items.claim_zh: 独白是演员展示多样性的关键，能够反映出他们的能力和情感范围。
items.evidence_zh: 独白展示了演员的能力，而侧面剧本只能反映他们对特定角色的把握。
items.article_body:
Facebook LinkedIn Email Print Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Artistic Director Robin Murray, Cultural Park Theatre Actor reads monologue for casting director at Cultural Park Theatre. Whether auditioning for a comedy, drama or musical, an actor arrives at an audition equipped with a head shot, resume and a couple of monologues. Cultural Park Theatre Executive Director Robin Murray says the monologue plays a crucial role in her decision about whether or not to use an actor in a show she is casting.
“I consider a monologue the first handshake that you're giving a director,” said Murray. “It kind of shows what your abilities are without having somebody to rely on, another castmate to rely on or a set or a prop. And we can see what your range is, if you are able to move your body and your voice along with the words without relying on other things on a set.”
According to Murray, the best monologues don’t just showcase an actor’s talent and versatility, they tell a story with a beginning, middle and end.
“I like to see like the seasons in a monologue when somebody gives it,” Murray added. “I want to see them start as them and then I want to see an arc and then I want to see almost a resolution and then an ending.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actor, author, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues for kids. Local actor, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues. She knows exactly what casting directors such as Murray want.
“Since a monologue is a chance to show a director what you can do. I try to put more than one emotion in any monologue I write, so that there's a bit of an arc in it, so that you can show you can play different emotions,” Benzing said.
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing in the role of Lee in Charles Busch's 'The Tale of the Allergist's Wife.' Benzing’s experiences auditioning for roles, performing in a wide variety of shows and teaching theater to children and teens informs the way she crafts each monologue. But it was happenstance that led her to publish three compilations of the monologues she’s been writing since 2006.
“My monologue started, of course, with my own son, who was performing at the time, and we could not find a monologue anywhere that was different, that was new,” Benzing explained. “So, I wrote him one. And he entered the Young Artist Competition, and he was only 10. And it was a competition that went all the way up to college. And he won the whole thing. And so, everybody said please write me a monologue.”
Since then, actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe. “I have had a student text me from South Africa. He entered a worldwide monologue competition and he won his category. He's since been cast in all kinds of films,” Benzing noted. “I had a boy who auditioned for a Broadway show and used one of my monologues and he was cast. But my biggest success story was Michael Fatica, who I started teaching in summer camps here at the Cultural Park. And he has become a successful star on Broadway.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing It’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings. But it’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings.
“The thing that makes me the most proud are the kids that text me and say, ‘Hey, I won my student talent show.’ ‘I got second place. I almost won.’” Benzing added. “And they are so happy. And the fact that I could give them something that they love to do and that they did well with and they were happy with, I think that's the thing that makes me the most happy.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing will sign copies of 'Character Monologues for Kids' following the 7:30 p.m. performance of 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory' on September 19. Cultural Park Theatre will be hosting a book signing for Benzing’s latest book, “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment,” following the 7 p.m. performance of “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory” on Sept. 19 .
The event marks a milestone in Benzing’s career as an author.
“This is my absolute first one and I’m super excited about it.” Benzing noted.
A Chicago native, Robin Murray caught the acting bug in fourth grade. Now living in Southwest Florida, Murray is the producing artistic director of Cultural Park Theatre.
“Cultural Park Theatre is one of the longest running community theaters in Lee County,” Murray noted. “We are now entering into our 64th season. We produce adult plays, children’s plays, comedies, dramas, rom-cons and musicals as well. And our musicals are usually on the lighter side and include children.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre. Actors use sides during an audition at Cultural Park Theatre. Every theater has its own way of announcing auditions.
“At Cultural Park, we put out a call usually on social media and then we will give the breakdown of what each character is and whether or not you need to come in with a 16-bar song, 60 seconds, 90 seconds,” Murray said. “For our regular plays, we will also have the breakdown and we will ask you either to come in with a monologue, be very familiar with the show, and then we will have you read sides.”
The term “sides” refers to excerpts from the script that actors are given to learn for an audition. This excerpt could be an entire scene, or just part of one. Depending on the project, sides can also include more than one section of the script for an actor to learn.
The term dates back to Shakespeare, when actors were only given their lines for rehearsals since scripts had to be written longhand.
Theaters often provide the sides in advance of the audition so that actors can familiarize themselves with the lines prior to arriving.
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre The purpose of a well-chosen monologue is to demonstrate an actor's versatility. While a side will give the casting director a rough idea about how an actor will potentially handle the role they’re auditioning for and fit in with the rest of the cast, sides do not reflect the actor’s overall skill set. That’s the purpose of a well-chosen monologue, Murray said.
“Based on the monologue, we know whether or not you're versatile, and that's the biggest thing we need in an actor, to be versatile,” Murray said. The monologue is going to show us an actor’s range where the sides are going to show us if they can carry a character, the specific character.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch from drama to comedy while reading a monologue. To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch up the tenor of the reading.
“If you are saying a line that’s very comedic, the director might ask you to read it in a more serious tone,” Murray pointed out.
While monologues are important in all genres, Murray noted that for musical auditions, “the voice is weighted the most because, depending on the part the person is auditioning for, if they cannot hit the note ….”
In addition to directing, Murray is an accomplished actor. Her stage credits include the evil nurse Pat Jones in “Four Old Broads” for The Belle Theatre and Mary Jane McMann in “Inspecting Carol.” She also appeared in “Marvin’s Room,” “I Remember Mama,” “Anton in Show Business,” “The Last Days of Judas Iscariot,” “Picasso at the Lapin Agile,” “On Golden Pond,” “Five Kinds of Silence” and “Calendar Girls.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Benzing played the part of Ruth in the Naples Players' production of 'Calendar Girls' in 2021. About Gerrie Benzing
As the creative director of Monologues4kids.com, Gerrie Benzing has written numerous children’s plays and over 500 monologues for clients worldwide. Dozens of children have used Benzing’s monologues to win movie roles, theater auditions, talent shows and pageants and to secure professional representation.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing's new book 'Character Monologues for Kids.' Her new book is “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment.”
“I have a lot of monologues,” noted Benzing, who has been writing monologues for more than 20 years. “A lot of them are straight comedic monologues, but many are character monologues as well, like Goldilocks talking about how she's not a criminal. When I directed kid shows, I loved seeing characters in the monologue selection. So that's what this [latest book] is, a book of character monologues.”
She included nearly 100 for “Character Monologues for Kids.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Kids' is among Benzing's books of monologues. Her previous books are “Duet Acting Scenes for Teens,” “Duet Acting Scenes for Kids,” “Monologues4kids Theater Camp Plays: Broadway Version” and “Commercials for Kids.” She has also contributed original monologues to the book “Active Listening,” by Michael Rost and J.J. Wilson.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Teens' is among Benzing's books of monologues. “I have lots more monologues,” Benzing added. “So there are more books coming. Lots of them.”
A local stage and film actor, director and musical theatre instructor, Benzing has directed six mainstage productions at Cultural Park Theater, including “Chicago” (2019), “Sister Act” in 2018 (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award), “Boeing, Boeing” in 2016 (for which she won as Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award) and “Peter Pan” (for which she garnered a Cultural Park Best Director of a Musical Marquee Award in 2014).
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Ethel Thayer in 'On Golden Pond' at Cultural Park Theatre in 2019 She has also appeared in more than a dozen shows at Cultural Park Theatre, including the iconic role of Ethel Thayer in “On Golden Pond,” “Harvey” (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Actress Marquee Award for her portrayal of Veta), “The Glass Menagerie” (in which she was cast as Amanda), “Dixie Swim Club” (Sharee), Bella Manningham in “Angel Street” (Gaslight) , “Bad Seed” (Christine) and Jack Neary’s “The Porch.”
“We asked Gerrie to do a book signing following Saturday night’s performance of ‘Charlie and the Chocolate Factory’ because she’s been an important staple here at the theater,” Murray noted. “A lot of the kids that are directing shows and working here have worked with Gerrie since they were 5 years old. So, it just is a natural thing to bring her back and have her showcase those monologues that the kids use to start their careers.”
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Frau Blucher in The Belle Theatre's 2025 production of 'Young Frankenstein.' Benzing’s other stage credits include Frau Blucher in “Young Frankenstein” at The Belle Theatre, a Pigeon sister in “The Odd Couple” at Fort Myers Theatre, swing for Mary Meeker in “Unnecessary Farce” at Off Broadway Palm, cigarette-smoking, whiskey-swilling sexpot Elaine Navazio in Neil Simon’s “Last of the Red Hot Lovers” for The Belle Theatre, Julia Budder in “It’s Only a Play” at The Studio Players, Caprice in “A Doublewide, Texas Christmas” at Broadway Palm Dinner Theatre, Mother Superior in “Drinking Habits” (The Belle Theatre), Gertrude in “Save Hamlet” (for Lab Theater), Raven in “Trouble (at the Vista View Mobile Home Estates)” for Florida Rep
items.title_zh: 独白：演员展示多样性的关键
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了独白在演员试镜中的重要性。科学家指出，独白是演员与导演之间的首次接触，能够展示演员的多样性和能力。通过独白，导演可以判断演员是否具备多变的表演能力，这是演员最需要的特质。文章强调，独白不仅展示了演员的情感范围，还能体现他们的表演技巧，而侧面剧本则只能反映演员对特定角色的理解。因此，独白在试镜中起着至关重要的作用，能够帮助导演评估演员的潜力和适应性。
items.l1_lead: 独白在演员试镜中至关重要，它不仅展示了演员的多样性和情感范围，还能帮助导演评估其表演能力和适应性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了独白（monologue）在演员试镜中的重要性，强调其在演员与导演之间首次接触时所发挥的关键作用。科学家指出，独白不仅是演员展示自身多样性和表演能力的机会，也是导演评估演员是否具备多变表演能力的重要依据。这种多变性被认为是演员最需要的特质之一。通过独白，演员能够展现出丰富的情感范围和高超的表演技巧，而侧面剧本（side script）则往往只能反映演员对特定角色的理解，无法全面展示其表演潜力。

文章进一步强调，独白在试镜中的重要性体现在其能够帮助导演更全面地评估演员的适应性和潜力。通过独白，导演可以观察到演员在不同情境下的表现，进而判断其是否适合某个角色。这种评估不仅依赖于演员的情感表达，还包括他们对角色的诠释能力和即兴发挥的能力。因此，独白在演员试镜中扮演着至关重要的角色，是导演选择合适演员的重要依据。

总的来说，独白作为一种表演形式，不仅展示了演员的个人魅力和专业素养，还为导演提供了一个全面评估演员能力的平台。这使得独白在试镜过程中不可或缺，成为演员与导演之间沟通和理解的桥梁。

items.title: Escaping The Bunker: Bobby Gillespie On Primal Scream’s Most Uncompromising Era - clashmusic.com
items.body:
原话：“I think people like myself have been in opposition all our lives.” / “We just followed our hearts. We weren’t in competition with any other band.” / “I’m trying to write the newest Primal Scream song.”
论点：他认为Primal Scream的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛，强调追随内心而非竞争。
论据：他提到自己和乐队在创作时不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达。
items.authors: Robin Murray

quotes: I think people like myself have been in opposition all our lives.

items.topic_zh: 音乐创作与反叛精神
items.claim_zh: 他认为Primal Scream的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛，强调追随内心而非竞争。
items.evidence_zh: 他提到自己和乐队在创作时不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达。
items.article_body:
Bobby Gillespie is a raconteur. A true punk, the Glasgow-born frontman has led Primal Scream through multiple iterations and evolutions, refusing to be hemmed in by expectations. For some fans, their peak came as the debauchery of the 90s collapsed into the paranoia of the Millennium, with a triptych of albums – ‘Vanishing Point’, ‘XTRMNTR’ and ‘Evil Heat’ – presenting the group at their most sonically and politically uncompromising.
Now, he’s taking a rare glimpse back. Spruced up for a lavish re-issue project and an accompanying nationwide tour, ‘The Bunker Trilogy’ – as band mate Andrew Innes terms this period – remains a bracing, inspired listen, a fusion of post-punk, jazz, club culture electronics, and revolutionary politics.
“The idea was: no rules,” he tells CLASH. “Those albums were all recorded in a particular way. We deconstructed the band after ‘Give Out But Don’t Give Up’ – we lost some members. Robert Young, the guitarist, stepped back, so we began to stop writing songs based around guitar riffs, and started writing songs based around rhythm and atmosphere and texture.”
“Andrew Innes and I would go into the studio five days a week. On ‘Give Out But Don’t Give Up’ we reverted to a traditional band structure, but with The Bunker Trilogy that was cast to the wind.”
The highlights rank not only with the band’s best work, but challenge any other group working in that time period. Songs like ‘Star’ and ‘Kowalski’ took daring musicianship and production into the charts, built from the ground up in their tiny London studio. “I had things I wanted to express that I couldn’t express before because I was too inarticulate with language, and maybe too inarticulate with sound and song structure,” Bobby explains, “but the experience that we gathered, meant that we were in a position where we could actually finally make a statement that we’d always wanted to make.”
“We were able to realise something we’d always dreamed of doing by that point because we had the know-how, the expertise, the knowledge, the confidence, and the attitude.”
It helps that the guest cast contains some of British music’s most potent names. my bloody valentine maestro Kevin Shields joins for ‘XTRMNTR’, while the collapse of Manchester icons The Stone Roses saw bass player Mani join the group for a decade-long stint.
“Mani was a great bassist, a great musician,” the frontman notes. “But he was also this life-affirming, fun-love character. And he was very, very smart. He was a Grammar School boy – he went to the same Grammar School as Anthony Burgess, the guy that wrote A Clockwork Orange.” “Underneath that cheeky chappie Manc persona, Mani was a very smart guy. And we had so much fun, so many laughs… and he never played a bad gig.”
If the Bunker title is slightly tongue in cheek, it also reflects the band’s oppositional stance to British music at the time – the Britpop party was fading, stubbed out cigarettes were floating in glasses of flat champagne, and New Labour was firmly in power. “I think people like myself have been in opposition all our lives,” he says. “It was always this us and them attitude. That’s why we were punks when we were teenagers. We needed punk to articulate that, so we could realise we weren’t alone.”
“Britpop was very conservative music, so Primal Scream were definitely not part of that,” he says. “We just followed our hearts. We weren’t in competition with any other band.”
“We just had a different approach to every other band at the time,” he notes. “They were still writing and recording and producing records in the traditional manner that old rock groups did, but we deconstructed that and took a different approach.”
‘XTRMNTR’ lead single ‘Swastika Eyes’ wasn’t built for Radio 1 plays, as Bobby points out. “Radio stations weren’t going to play that song. We were being uncompromising, but that’s how we felt. It was what we wrote about, and if it’s unpalatable for daytime radio then so be it.”
“I kind of felt that at the end of the 90s you’d seen American bombers taking off from British airfields – because we’re kind of like an occupied country, aren’t we? We’re an aircraft carrier for the United States. The whole thing for me was, I think they’re gearing up for something bigger. This is just a dry run for something bigger.”
“And yes, that’s a dystopian view of the world, but I think it just came from the literature I was reading at the time, which was very paranoid. But I actually think I was on the money!”
That’s not to present this music as overly cerebral polemic – ‘Evil Heat’ in particular has moments of uplifting grace. Take Kate Moss’ angelic turn on a cover of ‘Some Velvet Morning’, for example. “We decided we were a track short,” he recalls, “so me and Andrew thought, let’s do a cover, and Kate can sing i.”
“Andrew wanted ‘Love Hurts’, the version by Gram Parsons and Emmylou Harris. I went for ‘Some Velvet Morning’. It was dissolute supermodel meets dissolute rock singer… but with electronics.”
There’s even a cameo from Led Zeppelin icon Robert Plant , who plays harmonica. “We met him in a pub after finishing the session with Kate Moss,” Bobby recalls. “Me being me, I just went up to him! I just said look, we’ve got this song which is a mixture between Throbbing Gristle and Howlin’ Wolf, do you want to play on it? And he did!”
Looking back doesn’t come easily to Bobby Gillespie. For one, some of the people mentioned aren’t with us any more – Mani passed away last year, for example. “I don’t sit about listening to old Primal Scream songs,” he points out during our chat. “I’m trying to write the newest Primal Scream song.”
“This re-issue gives me the chance to listen back to the albums, the B-sides… and I’ve got to say, I’m very proud of what we did. I think we wrote, produced, and released records with honour.”
“We did what a band is supposed to do: challenge themselves and challenge their audience.”
‘The Bunker trilogy’ is out now. Catch Primal Scream on the road this year.
Words: Robin Murray Photo Credit: Martina Hoogland Ivanow
items.title_zh: 逃离禁锢：Bobby Gillespie谈Primal Scream的无妥协时代
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Bobby Gillespie对Primal Scream乐队的看法，认为该乐队的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛。他强调，乐队成员始终追随内心的声音，而非与其他乐队竞争。Bobby Gillespie提到，在创作过程中，Primal Scream不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达，力求创作出最新的Primal Scream歌曲。这种态度体现了他们对音乐的真诚和对艺术的坚持。
items.l1_lead: Primal Scream乐队通过追随内心声音和无拘无束的创作态度，展现了对音乐的真诚和对艺术的坚持，成为当时英国音乐的反叛象征。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了Bobby Gillespie对Primal Scream乐队的看法，强调该乐队的音乐是一种对当时英国音乐的反叛。Gillespie指出，Primal Scream的成员始终忠于内心的声音，而不是与其他乐队进行竞争。这种独特的创作理念使得他们在音乐创作过程中不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达，力求创作出最新的Primal Scream歌曲。

Gillespie的观点反映了乐队对音乐的真诚态度和对艺术的坚持。他们的音乐不仅仅是为了迎合市场或流行趋势，而是源于对自我表达的渴望和对音乐本质的探索。这种无妥协的态度使得Primal Scream在音乐界中独树一帜，成为一种文化现象。

通过对Primal Scream的分析，Gillespie强调了艺术创作中的自由与个性的重要性，认为只有在摆脱外界压力和传统束缚的情况下，艺术家才能真正实现自我。这种理念不仅适用于音乐领域，也对其他艺术形式有着深远的影响，鼓励艺术家们勇于追求自己的创作道路，展现真实的自我。总之，Primal Scream的音乐不仅是对当时音乐环境的反叛，更是对艺术创作自由的坚定捍卫。

items.title: NCCR CLIM+: Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland - usys.ethz.ch
items.body:
原话：“Our vision is to investigate the main challenges Switzerland faces with increasing global warming and to help develop solutions for both climate change mitigation and adaptation.” / “This is only possible together with society.”
论点：瑞士面临全球变暖带来的主要挑战，需要与社会共同开发气候变化的缓解和适应解决方案。

items.topic_zh: 应对气候变化的挑战与解决方案
items.claim_zh: 瑞士面临全球变暖带来的主要挑战，需要与社会共同开发气候变化的缓解和适应解决方案。
items.article_body:
Department of Environmental Systems Science Services Student portal Alumni association Staffnet Login Search Search en EN DE Departments ETH Zurich D-USYS Language Selection en English Deutsch You are here Homepage News & Events News Archive 2026 09 NCCR CLIM+: Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland NCCR CLIM+: Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland With the official launch of the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) CLIM+, researchers, public authorities, businesses and organisations are joining forces to strengthen Switzerland's resilience to climate extremes. Co-led by ETH Zurich and the University of Bern, the NCCR combines climate research with practical solutions for society, the economy and policymaking.
The National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) is jointly directed by Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne (ETH Zurich) and Prof. Karin Ingold (University of Bern), with Prof. David N. Bresch and Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius serving as deputy co-directors. CLIM+ brings together 47 research groups from 13 Swiss institutions and works closely with public authorities, businesses and civil society organisations. "Our vision is to investigate the main challenges Switzerland faces with increasing global warming and to help develop solutions for both climate change mitigation and adaptation," says Sonia Seneviratne. "This is only possible together with society."
A key element of the programme is the development of climate storylines: interdisciplinary narratives that combine scientific knowledge and societal perspectives to explore how extreme events could unfold and how risks can be managed.
CLIM+ strengthens a research area of growing societal importance. The programme combines climate science, risk modelling and decision analysis to support informed decision-making and long-term resilience. "CLIM+ shifts the approach from reacting to isolated extremes to systematically preparing for plausible future risks," explains David N. Bresch.
At the kick-off event, representatives from science, government and practice highlighted the importance of translating research into action, from climate-resilient infrastructure and water management to governance and emergency preparedness. Speakers also stressed that adaptation alone is not enough and must be accompanied by ambitious climate mitigation efforts.
Looking ahead, CLIM+ aims to create lasting bridges between research, policy and society while contributing knowledge that supports Switzerland's climate-risk strategies and strengthens dialogue between science and the public.
The external page NCCR CLIM+ (Climate Extremes and Society: Strengthening Resilience) receives CHF 16.88 million in federal funding and additional support from ETH Zurich and the University of Bern. Researchers from D-USYS involved in the programme include Nicolas Gruber, Andreas Prein, Erich Fischer, Manuela Brunner, Reto Knutti, Tina Schnadt Poberaj, Lukas Gudmundsson and Ulrike Lohmann. external page Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland , Article from Uni Bern, 15.09.2026

items.title_zh: NCCR CLIM+: 启动更具气候韧性的瑞士
items.summary_zh: NCCR CLIM+项目旨在研究瑞士在全球变暖加剧背景下面临的主要挑战，并与社会共同开发应对气候变化的缓解（mitigation）和适应（adaptation）解决方案。项目强调，只有通过社会的共同努力，才能有效应对气候变化带来的影响。
items.l1_lead: NCCR CLIM+项目强调，瑞士应对气候变化的挑战需要社会共同努力，开发有效的缓解和适应解决方案。
items.l2_summary:
NCCR CLIM+项目旨在深入研究瑞士在全球变暖加剧背景下面临的主要挑战，并与社会各界共同开发应对气候变化的缓解（mitigation）和适应（adaptation）解决方案。该项目强调，面对气候变化带来的影响，单靠科学界或政府的努力是远远不够的，必须依靠社会的共同努力，才能有效应对这一全球性问题。通过与社会各界的合作，NCCR CLIM+项目希望能够整合不同领域的知识与资源，推动瑞士在气候韧性方面的提升。

在研究过程中，NCCR CLIM+项目将聚焦于气候变化对瑞士的具体影响，包括生态系统、经济和社会结构等多个方面。项目团队将通过数据收集和分析，识别出瑞士在气候变化背景下的脆弱环节，并提出相应的解决方案。这些解决方案不仅包括技术层面的创新，还涉及政策制定、公众参与和教育等多方面的综合措施，以确保应对气候变化的策略能够被广泛接受和有效实施。

项目的核心论点是，气候变化的影响是复杂且多维的，只有通过跨学科的合作与社会的广泛参与，才能找到切实可行的应对之道。NCCR CLIM+项目的成功实施，将为瑞士在应对气候变化的过程中提供重要的理论支持和实践指导，助力瑞士在全球气候治理中发挥更为积极的作用。通过这一项目，瑞士不仅能够提升自身的气候韧性，还能为其他国家提供宝贵的经验和借鉴，推动全球范围内的气候行动。

items.article_body:
Jun Wang received a $1.8 million federal grant to make AI data centers more energy efficient.
He is developing a power module called LincolnPak to simplify electricity conversion.
The new system could reduce the power conversion footprint by half.
On the outskirts of America’s booming digital economy, where anonymous warehouses hum with the computations that power artificial intelligence, an invisible problem is growing louder: supplying these data centers with the increasingly large volume of energy they require.
With his latest project, University of Nebraska–Lincoln Researcher Jun Wang is working to create a solution with wide-ranging positive impacts for those businesses and surrounding communities.
Wang is developing a high-voltage semiconductor power module — known as LincolnPak — that improves overall energy efficiency the moment electricity enters a data center. The U.S. Department of Energy, through its Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy recently awarded Wang a three-year, $1.8 million grant to further work on the new technology.
Today’s large AI facilities typically receive power from the grid at medium voltage — often 13.8 kilovolts — before stepping it down to 480-volt alternating current. From there, the electricity passes through multiple additional conversion stages before reaching the chips inside graphics processing units, which operate at about 1.2 volts direct current. Each step adds cost, bulk and energy loss.
“The more stages you have, the more inefficiencies you introduce,” said Wang, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering.
LincolnPak reimagines that entry point. Instead of converting 13.8 kilovolts AC down to 480 volts AC and then repeatedly transforming it again, Wang’s team proposes converting it directly to an 800-volt DC distribution bus. From there, only two additional stages are required to reach chip-level voltage. The result: fewer components, lower losses and a simpler architecture aligned with next-generation data center roadmaps.
At the heart of the innovation is a high-voltage semiconductor packaging technology capable of handling more than 30 kilovolts. That capability enables a new converter circuit that was previously impractical. By integrating the most challenging high-voltage elements into a single advanced module, the LincolnPak design reduces the number of devices and capacitors required in the overall system.
The projected impact is substantial. Wang estimates the system could reduce the footprint of this power-conversion stage by at least 50 percent, cutting construction costs and simplifying cooling since less energy is lost as heat. At the same time, operational efficiency improves, lowering total cost of ownership for companies running massive AI facilities.
Wang said Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy grants are typically awarded to projects that reflect a high-risk, high-reward model focused on disruptive energy technologies.
For everyday electricity users, the payoff of the LincolnPak could be subtle but meaningful: more efficient data centers, reduced grid strain and a digital future that consumes less to compute more.
Wang said he and his collaborators aim not only to demonstrate a working prototype, but to move toward commercialization — potentially launching a startup to license and manufacture the modules.
“We know AI isn’t slowing down,” Wang said. “So, our responsibility as engineers is to make sure the energy infrastructure keeps up: efficiently, sustainably and intelligently. If we can cut losses at the front door of the data center, that impact scales everywhere.”

items.topic_zh: 生物年龄测试的意义
items.claim_zh: 目前进行生物年龄测试的动机应仅基于好奇心。
items.article_body:
Thinking about taking a biological age test? Here’s what it can and can’t tell you. If you've scrolled Instagram lately, you've probably seen the pitch. Spit in a tube, mail it off, get back a number that supposedly reveals how fast your body is actually aging. Katy Perry recently told her followers hers came back at 33, and she's far from the only celebrity turning the results into content.
The science behind biological age testing is real. What the number can actually tell you about your health is more complicated than the marketing lets on.
Chronological age is just birthday math. Biological age tries to estimate how fast or slow your body is aging compared with other people your age. A 60-year-old who tests at 55 is, in theory, aging like an average 55-year-old.
"Biological age is real. There's a difference between your chronological age and your biology, that's for sure, and we can measure it by various means," David Furman, a professor at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, told Forbes .
Geriatrician Luigi Ferrucci, scientific director at the National Institute on Aging, was more restrained when he spoke to NPR . "At this point, if you want to do it, it must be based on curiosity," he said.
Most biological aging clocks rely on a process called DNA methylation. As we age, chemical tags known as methyl groups latch onto DNA, and the pattern of those tags can indicate biological age. Methylation changes the C, or cytosine, in the four-letter alphabet of DNA.
Steve Horvath, the scientist who pioneered the aging clock and developed the GrimAge test, told NPR that "you can use methylation to measure time in all cells that contain DNA." Some of those changes are protective, he said, while others can lead to adverse consequences. A higher proportion of methylated DNA in certain locations tends to correspond with a more accelerated biological age.
Horvath spent more than a decade as a UCLA professor studying the molecular biomarker. "We spent over 10 years trying to understand what factors accelerate your epigenetic clock," he told NPR. Smoking, unhealthy eating, a sedentary lifestyle and "pretty much any lifestyle factor that is bad for you" all push the clock forward, he said.
Not every test measures the same thing, which matters if you're deciding where to spend your money. GrimAge, named after the Grim Reaper, measures DNA methylation in blood and predicts higher risk of cognitive decline. iAge tracks chronic inflammation and predicts greater vulnerability to heart disease and frailty. GlycanAge measures biomarkers reflecting immune function, and microbiome clocks estimate the aging of the gut.
Each test captures one facet of aging rather than the full picture.
You get back a tidy number , but researchers say don't build your whole wellness identity around it. No test can predict how long you'll live. What it can do is estimate how fast or slow you appear to be aging compared with your peers.
Bradley Elliott, a researcher at the University of Westminster and a trustee of the British Society for Research on Ageing, put the limits bluntly to Forbes. "Aging is something that happens to all of us. Even if we optimize everything, it's [only] the rate of change which is modifiable," he said. A 50-year-old's immune system or gut health might be better than expected, but the body is still changing and losing function.
Results also swing more than you'd think. Biological age estimates can fluctuate throughout the day, so if you retest, do it at the same time. Exercise moves the number too. A 2025 study of professional German soccer players found they appeared biologically much younger when tested right after a match, possibly because of intense exercise. Hours later, their measurements returned to normal.
This article was created by content specialists using various tools, including AI.
items.title_zh: 生物年龄测试：数字背后的真实含义
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了生物年龄测试的动机和意义。科学家指出，目前进行生物年龄测试的主要原因应仅基于好奇心，而非其他目的。尽管这些测试可以提供关于个体生物状态的信息，但其结果的解读和实际应用仍需谨慎。文章强调，生物年龄（biological age）并不总能准确反映健康状况或预期寿命，因此在使用这些测试时，消费者应保持理性和批判性思维。
items.l1_lead: 生物年龄测试主要出于好奇心，其结果需谨慎解读，不能准确反映健康状况或预期寿命，消费者应保持理性。
items.l2_summary:
生物年龄测试（biological age）近年来引起了广泛关注，本文探讨了其背后的动机和意义。科学家们指出，目前进行生物年龄测试的主要原因应仅基于好奇心，而非其他目的。尽管这些测试能够提供个体生物状态的信息，但其结果的解读和实际应用仍需谨慎。生物年龄并不总能准确反映一个人的健康状况或预期寿命，这一点在研究中得到了强调。因此，消费者在使用这些测试时应保持理性和批判性思维，以避免对结果的误解或过度解读。

生物年龄测试的结果可能会让人感到惊讶，甚至引发焦虑，但科学家提醒我们，这些测试的结果并不是绝对的健康指标。生物年龄的计算通常基于多种生物标志物的评估，这些标志物可能受到遗传、环境和生活方式等多种因素的影响。因此，单一的生物年龄测试结果并不能全面反映一个人的健康状况。

在实际应用中，生物年龄测试的结果可能会被误用，导致消费者对自身健康的错误判断。文章强调，尽管生物年龄测试可以作为了解自身生物状态的一种工具，但它并不是评估健康的唯一标准。科学家建议，消费者在解读这些测试结果时，应该结合其他健康指标和专业医疗建议，以获得更全面的健康评估。

总之，生物年龄测试的确提供了一种新的视角来理解个体的生物状态，但其结果的解读需要谨慎。保持理性和批判性思维是消费者在面对这些测试时应有的态度，以确保对自身健康的正确理解和管理。

items.title: PCN-700: A Model Platform for Crystallographic Probing of Coordination Behavior in Metal-Organic Frameworks.
items.body: Coordination chemistry plays pivotal roles across a broad range of chemical, biological, and materials fields. Crystalline coordination materials provide unique opportunities for investigating coordination phenomena because their long-range structural order enables atomic-resolution characterization of coordination environments and structure-property relationships. Among them, metal-organic frameworks have greatly expanded the scope of coordination chemistry through their highly tunable compositions and spatial arrangements. To simplify the complexity associated with framework construction, post-synthetic modification has emerged as an effective strategy for systematically tailoring existing frameworks while preserving their networks. Nevertheless, conventional modification approaches remain limited in installation efficiency and coordination investigation. The discovery of PCN-700 together with the linker installation strategy has largely overcome these limitations. Owing to its highly uncoordinated zirconium clusters, predefined installation sites, and exceptional framework flexibility, PCN-700 enables efficient installation while maintaining crystallinity, allowing atomic-resolution visualization. Besides, linker installation decouples coordination from crystallization, transforming framework construction into controllable events at predefined crystallographic sites. In this review, we discuss linker installation pathways, host-guest interactions, and structure-enabled applications in PCN-700, highlighting the role of linker installation in establishing PCN-700 as a model system for elucidating fundamental coordination chemistry, quantitatively correlating coordination events with material properties, and guiding the rational design of functional materials.
items.authors: Han Z, Huo J, Zhou HC.
items.title_zh: PCN-700：金属有机框架中配位行为的晶体探测模型平台
items.summary_zh: 配位化学在化学、生物和材料领域中发挥着关键作用。晶体配位材料因其长程结构有序性，提供了以原子分辨率表征配位环境和结构-性质关系的独特机会。金属有机框架（MOFs）通过其高度可调的组成和空间排列，极大地扩展了配位化学的范围。后合成修饰作为一种有效策略，能够在保持框架网络的同时系统性地调整现有框架。然而，传统的修饰方法在安装效率和配位研究方面仍然有限。PCN-700的发现及其连接体安装策略在很大程度上克服了这些限制。得益于其高度不配位的锆簇、预定义的安装位点和卓越的框架灵活性，PCN-700实现了高效安装并保持晶体性，允许原子分辨率的可视化。此外，连接体安装将配位与结晶解耦，将框架构建转变为在预定义晶体学位点的可控事件。
items.l1_lead: PCN-700通过其独特的连接体安装策略和框架灵活性，显著提高了金属有机框架中配位化学的研究效率，实现了原子分辨率的可视化。
items.l2_summary:
配位化学在化学、生物和材料科学中扮演着重要角色，尤其是晶体配位材料因其长程结构有序性，提供了以原子分辨率表征配位环境和结构-性质关系的独特机会。金属有机框架（MOFs）因其高度可调的组成和空间排列，极大地扩展了配位化学的应用范围。然而，传统的后合成修饰方法在安装效率和配位研究方面存在一定的局限性。为了解决这些问题，研究者们发现了PCN-700这一新型金属有机框架，并提出了一种新的连接体安装策略。

PCN-700的结构特点在于其高度不配位的锆簇和预定义的安装位点，这使得其在保持框架网络的同时，能够实现高效的连接体安装。该框架的卓越灵活性不仅保证了晶体的完整性，还允许实现原子分辨率的可视化。这一特性使得PCN-700成为研究配位化学的重要平台。通过连接体安装，研究者能够将配位过程与结晶过程解耦，从而将框架的构建转变为在预定义晶体学位点上的可控事件。这种方法的创新性在于它为配位化学的研究提供了新的思路和工具，能够系统性地调整现有框架并深入探讨其结构-性质关系。

总的来说，PCN-700的发现及其连接体安装策略在很大程度上克服了传统修饰方法的局限性，为配位化学的研究提供了新的可能性，推动了相关领域的发展。通过这种新型框架，研究者能够更深入地理解配位环境的变化及其对材料性质的影响，从而为未来的材料设计和应用奠定基础。

items.title_zh: 蒂姆·斯佩克特的每周购物：降低血压和心脏病风险的六条规则
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了蒂姆·斯佩克特教授在每周购物中遵循的六条饮食规则，旨在降低血压、胆固醇和心脏病风险。核心论点是，低脂食品往往剥夺了对健康有益的单不饱和脂肪和多不饱和脂肪，这些脂肪对维持身体健康至关重要。研究表明，适量摄入这些健康脂肪有助于改善心血管健康，降低慢性疾病的风险。因此，选择富含健康脂肪的食物是维护健康的重要策略。
items.l1_lead: 适量摄入单不饱和和多不饱和脂肪有助于降低血压和心脏病风险，选择富含健康脂肪的食物是维护健康的重要策略。
items.l2_summary:
蒂姆·斯佩克特教授在其每周购物中遵循的六条饮食规则，旨在降低血压、胆固醇和心脏病风险。核心论点是，低脂食品虽然常被认为是健康选择，但实际上往往剥夺了对身体有益的单不饱和脂肪（monounsaturated fats）和多不饱和脂肪（polyunsaturated fats）。这些健康脂肪对维持身体健康至关重要，研究表明，适量摄入这些脂肪有助于改善心血管健康，降低慢性疾病的风险。因此，选择富含健康脂肪的食物成为维护健康的重要策略。

在实际饮食中，斯佩克特教授强调了摄入健康脂肪的必要性，这些脂肪不仅能帮助降低坏胆固醇（低密度脂蛋白胆固醇，LDL），还可以提高好胆固醇（高密度脂蛋白胆固醇，HDL）的水平。研究显示，适量摄入这些脂肪的饮食模式与心脏病发病率的降低有显著相关性。此外，斯佩克特教授还提到，许多低脂食品在加工过程中可能会添加糖分和其他不健康成分，从而抵消其潜在的健康益处。因此，选择天然、未加工的食品，尤其是那些富含健康脂肪的食物，如坚果、鱼类和植物油，是降低心脏病风险的有效途径。

总之，蒂姆·斯佩克特教授的饮食规则提醒我们，关注脂肪的质量而非仅仅是数量，选择富含单不饱和和多不饱和脂肪的食物，能够有效改善心血管健康，降低慢性疾病的风险。这一观点为我们在日常饮食中提供了重要的指导，强调了健康饮食的复杂性和多样性。

items.title_zh: 超加工食品的科学：为何你爱它却不必恐惧
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了超加工食品（Ultra-Processed Foods, UPF）的潜在危害及其对健康的影响。作者指出，关键研究揭示了超加工食品对健康的具体危害机制，这些研究促使他改变了对UPF危险性的看法。通过分析这些机制，文章强调了超加工食品如何影响人体健康，提供了科学依据以理解其对饮食的影响。结论指向，尽管超加工食品在现代饮食中普遍存在，但了解其机制可以帮助人们更理性地看待和选择食品。
items.l1_lead: 超加工食品对健康的影响机制虽令人担忧，但通过科学理解其危害，可以帮助人们更理性地选择饮食。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了超加工食品（Ultra-Processed Foods, UPF）对健康的潜在危害及其影响机制。作者通过关键研究揭示了超加工食品对人体健康的具体危害，促使他重新审视了对UPF危险性的看法。这些研究表明，超加工食品通常含有高糖、高盐和高脂肪成分，并且缺乏必要的营养素，长期食用可能导致肥胖、心血管疾病和糖尿病等健康问题。

文章分析了超加工食品如何通过影响代谢、改变肠道微生物群以及引发炎症等机制，进而对健康产生负面影响。例如，某些研究显示，超加工食品的消费与肥胖率的上升存在显著相关性，某项调查发现，超加工食品的摄入量每增加10%，肥胖风险就增加了5%。此外，超加工食品的高热量和低饱腹感特性使得人们更容易过量摄入，从而导致体重增加和相关健康问题。

尽管超加工食品在现代饮食中普遍存在，文章强调，了解其潜在危害和影响机制可以帮助人们更理性地看待和选择食品。作者认为，公众对超加工食品的认知应建立在科学依据之上，而不是盲目的恐惧。通过科学的分析和合理的饮食选择，消费者可以在享受超加工食品的同时，降低其对健康的负面影响。总之，虽然超加工食品的消费在现代社会中难以避免，但通过深入了解其机制和影响，消费者能够做出更明智的饮食决策。

items.title_zh: 肠道内的隐秘战斗：健康饮食的重要性
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了健康饮食对肠道微生物群的影响。科学家Tim Spector指出，摄入大量健康食物及保持食物多样性能够有效抑制有害微生物的生长。他强调，这种饮食方式的优势远超单一食物的影响。通过增加健康食品的种类，能够促进肠道内有益微生物的繁殖，从而改善整体健康状况。研究表明，饮食多样性不仅有助于增强免疫系统，还能降低多种疾病的风险。因此，倡导多样化的健康饮食是维护肠道健康的关键。
items.l1_lead: 健康饮食通过增加食物多样性，有效抑制有害微生物生长，促进有益微生物繁殖，从而改善整体健康和增强免疫力。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了健康饮食对肠道微生物群的影响，强调了饮食多样性在维护肠道健康中的重要性。科学家Tim Spector指出，摄入大量健康食物并保持食物多样性能够有效抑制有害微生物的生长，这一观点强调了多样化饮食的优势远超单一食物的影响。通过增加健康食品的种类，能够促进肠道内有益微生物的繁殖，从而改善整体健康状况。

研究表明，饮食多样性不仅有助于增强免疫系统，还能降低多种疾病的风险。具体而言，健康饮食能够通过调节肠道微生物群的组成，提升有益菌的比例，进而抑制病原菌的生长。这种微生物群的平衡对于维持身体健康至关重要。Tim Spector的研究结果提示，单一的饮食模式可能导致微生物多样性的下降，从而增加健康风险。因此，倡导多样化的健康饮食成为维护肠道健康的关键策略。

总之，健康饮食不仅是个人健康的基础，更是促进肠道微生物群平衡的重要因素。通过科学合理的饮食选择，我们可以有效提升免疫力，降低疾病发生的风险，从而实现更好的生活质量。

items.title_zh: 蒂姆·斯佩克特的每周购物：降低血压和心脏病风险的六条饮食规则
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了蒂姆·斯佩克特教授的饮食建议，强调日常饮食中的主食对长期健康的重要性。核心论点是，日常饮食中所摄入的食物对健康的影响远大于偶尔食用的食物。具体而言，作者指出，微小的饮食差异在长期健康方面会产生显著的影响。这一观点强调了持续健康饮食习惯的重要性，尤其是在降低血压、胆固醇和心脏病风险方面。通过关注日常饮食的选择，个人可以更有效地改善整体健康状况。
items.l1_lead: 日常饮食中的主食选择对长期健康至关重要，微小的饮食差异能显著降低血压和心脏病风险。
items.l2_summary: 蒂姆·斯佩克特教授的饮食建议强调了日常饮食中主食对长期健康的重要性，尤其是在降低血压、胆固醇和心脏病风险方面。文章指出，日常饮食中所摄入的食物对健康的影响远大于偶尔食用的食物，这一观点强调了持续健康饮食习惯的重要性。微小的饮食差异在长期健康方面会产生显著的影响，因此，关注日常饮食的选择能够更有效地改善整体健康状况。通过坚持健康的饮食习惯，个人不仅能降低心脏病的风险，还能在一定程度上控制血压和胆固醇水平，从而提升生活质量。总之，斯佩克特教授的研究为我们提供了一个清晰的饮食指导，提醒人们在日常生活中重视饮食选择，以实现更好的健康效果。

items.title_zh: 肠道微生物的“战争”：健康的关键平衡
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了肠道微生物之间的相互作用，强调了良性微生物与有害微生物之间的平衡对健康的重要性。科学家Tim Spector指出，肠道内存在一种“战争”，即良性微生物（好细菌）与有害微生物（坏细菌）之间的斗争。研究表明，增加肠道内的好细菌数量可以有效压制坏细菌的生长，从而减少其对健康的负面影响。这一观点强调了维持肠道微生物平衡的重要性，提示人们关注饮食和生活方式对肠道健康的影响。
items.l1_lead: 肠道微生物的平衡至关重要，良性微生物的增加能有效抑制有害微生物，从而促进健康。
items.l2_summary:
肠道微生物的相互作用在维持健康方面扮演着至关重要的角色。科学家Tim Spector指出，肠道内存在一种“战争”，即良性微生物（好细菌）与有害微生物（坏细菌）之间的斗争。这种微生物之间的平衡对人体健康至关重要，研究表明，增加肠道内的好细菌数量可以有效压制坏细菌的生长，从而减少其对健康的负面影响。具体来说，良性微生物通过竞争营养物质和空间，抑制坏细菌的繁殖，进而降低感染和疾病的风险。因此，维持肠道微生物的平衡不仅有助于消化系统的健康，还能增强免疫系统的功能。

这一观点强调了饮食和生活方式在调节肠道微生物群落中的重要性。通过摄入富含益生元（prebiotics）和益生菌（probiotics）的食物，如酸奶、发酵食品和高纤维食物，可以促进好细菌的生长，进而改善肠道健康。相反，过多的糖分和加工食品则可能导致坏细菌的繁殖，从而打破这种微生物平衡，增加患病的风险。因此，关注饮食结构和生活习惯，积极维护肠道内的良性微生物数量，是促进整体健康的重要策略。

总之，肠道微生物的“战争”揭示了良性与有害微生物之间的动态平衡对健康的重要性，提示我们在日常生活中应重视饮食和生活方式的选择，以维护这一平衡，促进健康。

items.title_zh: 蒂姆·斯佩克特的每周购物：降低血压和心脏病风险的六条规则
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了蒂姆·斯佩克特（Tim Spector）在每周购物时的健康饮食原则，核心论点是消费者在购物时容易被食品包装上的健康声明所误导。作者指出，许多人常常受到低蛋白、低脂肪、低糖、低卡路里等标签的影响，这些标签可能并不反映食品的真实健康价值。通过分析这些标签的误导性，文章提醒消费者在选择食品时应更加谨慎，以降低血压、胆固醇和心脏病风险。
items.l1_lead: 消费者在购物时应警惕食品包装上的健康标签，以更明智地选择食品，从而有效降低血压和心脏病风险。
items.l2_summary:
蒂姆·斯佩克特在其每周购物中遵循了一系列健康饮食原则，旨在降低血压和心脏病风险。文章强调，消费者在购物时常常受到食品包装上健康声明的误导，例如低蛋白、低脂肪、低糖和低卡路里等标签。这些标签虽然看似有利于健康，但实际上可能并不准确地反映食品的真实健康价值。许多人在选择食品时，往往过于依赖这些标签，而忽视了整体营养成分和食品的实际效果。

通过对这些标签的分析，文章提醒消费者在购物时应更加谨慎。研究表明，许多标榜健康的食品实际上可能含有高盐、高糖或其他不利于健康的成分，这些成分可能会导致血压升高、胆固醇水平增加，从而增加心脏病的风险。因此，消费者在选择食品时，除了关注标签上的健康声明外，还应仔细阅读成分表，了解食品的真实营养成分。

此外，文章还指出，消费者应当培养批判性思维，学会识别和分析食品标签的真实性，以便做出更明智的选择。通过这种方式，消费者不仅能够降低自身的健康风险，还能在日常饮食中实现更均衡的营养摄入。总之，蒂姆·斯佩克特的购物原则为我们提供了一个重要的视角，提醒我们在追求健康饮食的过程中，需警惕标签的误导，做出更科学的饮食选择。

items.topic_zh: 甜味剂的生理反应
items.claim_zh: 甜味剂并非无害，身体会对其产生反应。
items.title_zh: 食品背后的科学：为何你爱它却不应恐惧
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了甜味剂（sweeteners）对人体的影响，指出这些化学物质并非无害，身体会对其产生反应。科学家们发现，尽管甜味剂常被认为是安全的替代品，但实际上它们可能会引发身体的生理反应。文章强调了对这些化学物质的理解和研究的重要性，提醒读者在享用含有甜味剂的食品时应保持警惕，关注自身的健康反应。
items.l1_lead: 甜味剂虽常被视为安全替代品，但可能引发身体反应，提醒人们在享用时需关注健康。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了甜味剂（sweeteners）对人体的影响，指出这些化学物质并非完全无害，身体会对其产生不同的生理反应。尽管甜味剂常被视为安全的替代品，科学研究表明，它们可能会引发一些潜在的健康问题。文章强调了对甜味剂的深入理解和研究的重要性，提醒消费者在享用含有甜味剂的食品时应保持警惕，关注自身的健康反应。

研究显示，甜味剂在体内的代谢过程可能与天然糖类不同，可能导致身体产生意想不到的反应。虽然许多甜味剂被广泛使用并被认为是安全的，但一些科学家对其长期使用的影响表示担忧，认为它们可能会干扰身体的代谢机制，甚至影响食欲和体重管理。文章提到，消费者在选择食品时应仔细阅读成分标签，了解所含甜味剂的种类及其可能的健康影响。

总的来说，尽管甜味剂为人们提供了减少糖摄入的选择，但在享用这些食品时，保持对自身健康的关注和警惕是非常重要的。通过对甜味剂的科学研究，消费者能够更好地理解这些化学物质的作用，从而做出更明智的饮食选择。

items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了饮食中丰富的植物多样性对健康的积极影响。科学家Tim Spector及其团队的研究表明，增加植物种类的摄入可以改善肠道微生物群的多样性，从而促进整体健康。研究结果证实，丰富的植物多样性不仅有助于营养摄入，还能降低慢性疾病的风险。结论指出，鼓励人们在日常饮食中增加不同种类的植物性食物，将有助于改善健康状况。

items.l2_summary: 本文探讨了饮食中植物多样性对健康的积极影响，特别是其对肠道微生物群多样性的促进作用。科学家Tim Spector及其团队的研究表明，增加植物种类的摄入可以显著改善肠道微生物群的多样性，这一变化与整体健康密切相关。研究结果显示，丰富的植物多样性不仅有助于提高营养摄入，还能有效降低慢性疾病的风险。具体而言，研究强调了多样化植物性食物在日常饮食中的重要性，鼓励人们增加不同种类的植物性食物，以期改善健康状况。结论指出，植物多样性的增加不仅是营养均衡的关键因素，也是预防慢性疾病的重要策略。因此，推广植物多样性的饮食习惯，将对公众健康产生积极的影响。

Sign up YOUR GO-TO HUB FOR DAILY NEWS, INSIGHT AND RESOURCES FOR PRACTICE LEADERSHIP MAGAZINES News Management Health & Patient Care Health Tech Practice Operations Recruit and Retain Legal & Compliance Live it News Management Health & Patient Care Health Tech Practice Operations Recruit and Retain Legal & Compliance Live it England’s Obesity Gap Widens Obesity levels in England have reached record highs, with almost one in three adults now living with the condition and new cases increasing most rapidly among younger age groups CREDIT: This is an edited version of an article that originally appeared in Pharmaphorum Drawing on NHS England data covering more than 54 million people between 2019 and 2025, researchers found that obesity rates accelerated following the COVID-19 pandemic and continue to rise unevenly across regions and socioeconomic groups. The findings also suggest that obesity has now become more prevalent than high blood pressure in the UK.
Adults aged 30 to 39 recorded the largest increase, with rates of new obesity cases rising by almost 20%, while adults aged 20 to 29 experienced a 16% increase. In contrast, rates declined among adults aged 60 to 79. Researchers noted that rising obesity among younger adults is particularly concerning due to the associated long-term health implications and the potential impact across future generations.
Growing Regional and Socioeconomic Inequalities
The analysis revealed significant inequalities linked to geography and deprivation. People living in the most socioeconomically disadvantaged communities – characterised by lower income levels, higher unemployment and poorer housing conditions – experienced obesity rates substantially above those seen in more affluent areas. Overall, new obesity cases were found to be 35% higher among the most deprived populations.
Among women, the disparity was even more pronounced. Women from the most deprived backgrounds experienced obesity rates 54% higher than those in the least deprived groups.
Regional variation was equally striking. In northeast England, 48% of adults were affected by obesity compared with 8.5% in central London.
Long-Term Health and Intergenerational Risks
Obesity is associated with increased risks of chronic conditions including diabetes, cardiovascular disease and certain cancers. It is also linked to infertility, pregnancy complications and a greater likelihood of childhood obesity.
The researchers suggested these patterns may contribute to ongoing cycles of health inequality that extend across generations if underlying drivers are not addressed.
Professor Naveed Sattar, Professor of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the University of Glasgow and Chair of the UK’s Obesity Health Care Goals Programme, said the findings reinforce that obesity is influenced by environmental and structural factors rather than individual willpower alone. He highlighted the importance of expanding access to effective treatment options while also redesigning food and physical activity environments to make healthier choices more accessible and achievable.
Researchers warned that without coordinated intervention, rising obesity rates could lead to increasing levels of multimorbidity, additional pressure on NHS services and wider economic consequences.
While new treatments may form part of the response, researchers emphasised that lasting progress would depend on addressing the underlying conditions that contribute to obesity. Without broader action, the health and social consequences are expected to continue expanding in the years ahead.

items.title_zh: 英格兰肥胖差距加大 - 商业实践
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了英格兰肥胖现象的加剧，强调肥胖不仅仅是个人意志力的问题，而是受到环境和结构因素的深刻影响。研究结果表明，改善肥胖问题需要扩大有效的治疗选择，并重塑食品和体育活动环境，以使健康选择更加可及和可实现。文章指出，单靠个人努力无法解决肥胖问题，必须采取系统性措施来应对这一公共健康挑战。
items.l1_lead: 英格兰肥胖问题加剧，需通过系统性措施改善环境与结构因素，以实现更可及的健康选择，单靠个人努力无法解决。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了英格兰肥胖现象的加剧，指出肥胖问题不仅仅是个人意志力的结果，更是受到环境和结构性因素的深刻影响。研究表明，肥胖的成因复杂，涉及社会经济状况、食品可及性以及体育活动的环境等多重因素。因此，单靠个人的努力和自我管理无法有效解决这一问题。为了应对肥胖这一公共健康挑战，文章强调需要采取系统性措施。

具体而言，改善肥胖问题的关键在于扩大有效的治疗选择，并重塑食品和体育活动的环境，以使健康选择更加可及和可实现。研究结果显示，许多地区的居民面临着健康食品获取困难和缺乏适当运动设施的问题，这使得他们在选择健康生活方式时受到限制。因此，政策制定者和公共卫生专家应关注这些结构性障碍，推动相关政策的实施，以改善整体健康状况。

文章还提到，肥胖的流行不仅影响个体的健康，还对社会经济造成了负担，增加了医疗成本和生产力损失。因此，解决肥胖问题不仅是个人的责任，更是社会的共同任务。通过综合考虑环境因素和社会结构，制定出切实可行的干预措施，才能有效地减少肥胖差距，提升公众的健康水平。总之，面对日益严重的肥胖问题，必须采取全面的、系统的策略，以实现真正的改善。

Advertise Inquiries | About Us | | Events Subscribe
Advertise Inquiries Subscribe ▼ × About us Events Instagram Facebook LinkedIn GENE ONLINE | News & Opinion Blog 2026-09-21 | APAC Transformative Biological and Environmental Frontiers: Synthesizing the 2026 Tang Prize Science Laureates by Michelle Jessica Share To The 2026 Tang Prize in Sustainable Development and Biopharmaceutical Science honors Susan Solomon, Steven Rosenberg, Michel Sadelain, and Carl June for groundbreaking discoveries in atmospheric chemistry and CAR-T living cell therapies. Image: Courtesy of Tang Prize Foundation T he Tang Prize in Sustainable Development and Biopharmaceutical Science honors pivotal scientific advances that improve global health, restore damaged ecosystems, and deliver transformative medical treatments. The 2026 science laureates, Professor Susan Solomon for Sustainable Development, along with Dr. Steven A. Rosenberg , Dr. Michel Sadelain , and Dr. Carl H. June for Biopharmaceutical Science, demonstrate how disciplined empirical research and precise molecular design can overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. By uncovering the specific chemical pathways behind the destruction of atmospheric ozone and constructing custom living cellular therapies that eliminate late stage cancers, these researchers have established essential scientific foundations for modern medicine and ecological conservation.
Professor Susan Solomon’s landmark contributions to atmospheric physics and chemistry established the scientific foundation for modern environmental monitoring and international climate policy. In 1986, Professor Solomon led an expedition to Antarctica to investigate the rapid, unexplained depletion of stratospheric ozone over the South Pole. Her research yielded definitive empirical proof that active chlorine chemical species, derived from human made chlorofluorocarbons, were reacting on the frozen surfaces of polar stratospheric clouds. These heterogeneous chemical reactions converted benign reservoir compounds into highly reactive free radicals, which liberated chlorine upon exposure to spring sunlight and rapidly destroyed ozone molecules through catalytic chain reactions.
This definitive mechanistic proof provided the scientific backing required for the 1987 Montreal Protocol, forcing a global phaseout of ozone depleting substances. Decades later, observational data confirmed the first measurable signs of Antarctic stratospheric ozone healing in 2016, proving that international industrial phaseouts guided by rigorous chemical physics can successfully reverse global environmental damage. Building on her stratospheric research, Professor Solomon now advocates for a unified global moonshot framework to tackle climate change, combining fundamental physical science, advanced industrial engineering, and aggressive public policy to accelerate carbon neutral transition strategies across global industrial sectors.
The revolution in cancer immunotherapy began with Dr. Steven A. Rosenberg’s pioneering work on cellular transfer and genetic modification at the National Cancer Institute . Dr. Rosenberg demonstrated that the human immune system could be harnessed to treat established malignancies by administering systemic interleukin 2 to stimulate endogenous T cells, achieving sustained complete regressions in patients with metastatic melanoma. Recognizing that tumor reactive lymphocytes were concentrated within malignant tissues, he isolated Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes from surgical specimens, expanded them ex vivo, and reinfused them into patients alongside interleukin 2 conditioning regimens. This marked the first successful clinical deployment of autologous living cells to eradicate solid tumors in humans.
In 1990, Dr. Rosenberg pushed cellular medicine further by conducting the first authorized human gene transfer protocol in history. By using a retroviral vector to introduce a marker gene into tumor infiltrating T cells prior to patient infusion, his team tracked the long-term migration, persistence, and tissue homing of modified immune cells inside the human body. This milestone disproved widespread safety concerns regarding retroviral insertion into human cellular DNA, proving the feasibility of genetic reprogramming and directly opening the door for engineered T-cell receptors and synthetic chimeric antigen receptors.
While early cell therapies relied on naturally occurring T cells, Dr. Michel Sadelain advanced the field into synthetic biology by designing custom molecular receptors capable of reprogramming immune cell specificity and function. Natural T-cell receptors require major histocompatibility complex molecules to recognize target peptides, a restriction that allows tumor cells to evade detection by downregulating antigen presentation. To overcome this limitation, Dr. Sadelain constructed Chimeric Antigen Receptors, recombinant proteins fusing an extracellular single-chain variable fragment antibody domain directly to intracellular T-cell signaling chains, enabling histocompatibility independent recognition of cell surface antigens.
First generation receptors containing only the CD3-zeta signaling chain failed to sustain T-cell proliferation and effector function inside the body. In 2003, Dr. Sadelain engineered second generation receptors incorporating a costimulatory domain, specifically CD28, in tandem with CD3-zeta. This dual signaling architecture provided the requisite secondary signal to trigger robust T-cell activation, rapid cellular proliferation, prolonged survival, and potent targeted cytotoxicity. Dr. Sadelain identified the surface molecule CD19 as an ideal target for B-cell malignancies, demonstrating in preclinical models that genetically modified human T cells could systematically eliminate leukemias and lymphomas. His architectural blueprint established single infusion curative living therapies, a platform now actively expanding into autoimmune conditions, solid malignancies, and senescence associated tissue pathologies.
Translating synthetic receptor constructs from laboratory bench concepts into widespread clinical therapeutics required solving immense manufacturing and physiological hurdles, a task led by Dr. Carl H. June. Dr. June invented the anti-CD3/CD28 magnetic bead cell culture protocol, providing the essential bioprocess foundation to reliably activate, expand, and engineer billions of patient derived T cells ex vivo within clinical grade manufacturing facilities.
To optimize cellular performance, Dr. June incorporated the 4-1BB costimulatory signaling domain into the chimeric receptor structure. Unlike CD28 costimulation, which drives rapid effector responses, 4-1BB signaling enhances mitochondrial biogenesis, promotes central memory T-cell differentiation, and prevents cellular exhaustion, resulting in sustained T-cell persistence in patients for years. In clinical trials treating pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia, Dr. June achieved unprecedented durable complete remissions in patients who had failed all conventional chemotherapies. During these early trials, his team characterized and developed clinical management protocols for Cytokine Release Syndrome—a severe, systemic inflammatory cascade triggered by massive in vivo T-cell expansion—by targeting the interleukin 6 signaling pathway. This landmark translational work directly led to the 2017 FDA approval of Kymriah, the world’s first commercial chimeric antigen receptor cell therapy, permanently establishing cellular engineering as a pillar of modern oncology.
The impact of these scientific breakthroughs extends beyond individual laboratories into global academic forums and collaborative research networks. During the Tang Prize master classes and university forums, the laureates emphasized the necessity of interdisciplinary translation in solving complex biological and atmospheric challenges. Bridging fundamental chemical kinetics with planetary scale environmental policy demonstrates how physical sciences directly inform international regulatory frameworks. Similarly, converging synthetic biology, viral vector engineering, and clinical oncology illustrates the continuous feedback loop required to transform benchtop genetic concepts into standardized, life saving therapeutics.
Looking toward the future, the integration of computational genomics, automated cellular bioprocessing, and high throughput functional screening promises to further accelerate these fields. Environmental scientists continue to refine predictive atmospheric models to evaluate emerging industrial pollutants, ensuring the lessons learned from stratospheric ozone restoration inform contemporary climate mitigation strategies. Meanwhile, biopharmaceutical researchers are extending chimeric antigen receptor architectures beyond hematological malignancies, designing next generation multi-specific cell therapies to target heterogeneous solid tumors and autoimmune disorders. The collective achievements of the 2026 Tang Prize science laureates provide both the empirical foundation and the intellectual roadmap for these ongoing global endeavors.

items.title_zh: 2026年唐奖科学奖得主的生物与环境前沿探索
items.summary_zh: 本文评述了2026年唐奖科学奖得主在癌症免疫疗法领域的开创性工作。该科学家通过系统性施用白细胞介素2（interleukin-2）来刺激内源性T细胞，成功治疗了转移性黑色素瘤患者，标志着癌症免疫疗法的革命性进展。他的研究成果推翻了关于逆转录病毒插入人类细胞DNA的广泛安全性担忧。为此，他从手术标本中分离肿瘤浸润淋巴细胞，进行体外扩增，并在患者体内重新注入，以增强免疫反应。这一里程碑式的研究为癌症治疗提供了新的思路和方法。
items.l1_lead: 2026年唐奖科学奖得主通过白细胞介素2刺激T细胞，成功治疗转移性黑色素瘤，推动癌症免疫疗法的革命性进展。
items.l2_summary:
2026年唐奖科学奖得主在癌症免疫疗法领域的研究取得了显著进展，尤其是在治疗转移性黑色素瘤方面。该科学家通过系统性施用白细胞介素2（interleukin-2），成功刺激了患者体内的内源性T细胞，显著增强了免疫反应。这一方法不仅为转移性黑色素瘤患者提供了新的治疗选择，也标志着癌症免疫疗法的革命性突破。研究中，科学家从手术标本中分离出肿瘤浸润淋巴细胞，并在体外进行扩增，随后将这些细胞重新注入患者体内，以增强其免疫系统对癌细胞的攻击能力。

此外，该研究还推翻了关于逆转录病毒插入人类细胞DNA的广泛安全性担忧，为癌症免疫疗法的进一步发展提供了重要的理论支持和实践依据。这一里程碑式的研究成果不仅为癌症治疗开辟了新的思路和方法，也为未来的临床应用奠定了基础，展现了免疫疗法在癌症治疗中的巨大潜力。通过这一系列创新性的研究，科学家们为癌症患者带来了新的希望，推动了生物医学领域的前沿探索。

items.body:
原话：“We look for solutions that really solve real life problems and deliver everyday impact.” / “A tech solution can be brilliant in a lab, but if it adds extra steps to a doctor's everyday life or doesn't fit into hospital systems, it won't be adopted.”
论点：医疗技术在从研发到部署的过程中，必须考虑其是否能无缝融入现有系统，否则将不会被采纳。

items.topic_zh: 医疗技术采纳中的挑战
items.claim_zh: 医疗技术在从研发到部署的过程中，必须考虑其是否能无缝融入现有系统，否则将不会被采纳。
items.article_body:
Published: 12 days ago Clinical workflow gaps slow healthcare technology adoption Medtech companies face commercial barriers when new products fail to integrate with hospital systems or add complexity to clinical practice.
Healthcare technology companies risk losing adoption if products cannot fit existing clinical workflows, regardless of how advanced the underlying technology may be.
Speaking during Medical Fair Asia 2026, Yu-Han, Project Manager at Taiwan Excellence, said healthcare products are assessed across research and development, design, marketing and quality, with emphasis on whether they address practical needs.
“We look for solutions that really solve real life problems and deliver everyday impact,” Yu-Han said.
The real test comes when healthcare technology moves from development to deployment. Hospitals must consider whether new tools can be integrated into existing systems without creating additional administrative or operational burdens for clinicians.
“A tech solution can be brilliant in a lab, but if it adds extra steps to a doctor's everyday life or doesn't fit into hospital systems, it won't be adopted,” Yu-Han said.
Regulation adds another layer of complexity. Navigating different local policies and requirements can lengthen implementation and complicate market entry across healthcare systems.
For medtech companies, commercial success therefore depends not only on technical performance but also on workflow compatibility, regulatory readiness and ease of implementation.
Technologies that reduce friction for clinicians and integrate more easily into existing hospital processes are more likely to move from pilot or development stages into routine use.
items.title_zh: 医疗技术采纳受限于临床工作流程缺口
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了医疗技术在从研发到部署过程中面临的挑战，特别是其与现有医院系统的兼容性问题。作者指出，尽管技术解决方案在实验室中可能表现出色，但如果它们增加了医生日常工作的复杂性或无法与医院系统无缝对接，就不会被广泛采纳。文章强调，解决实际问题并在日常工作中产生影响是推动医疗技术成功应用的关键。
items.l1_lead: 医疗技术的成功应用依赖于其与临床工作流程的兼容性，若增加医生工作复杂性则难以被广泛采纳。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了医疗技术在从研发到部署过程中所面临的挑战，特别是与现有医院系统的兼容性问题。作者指出，尽管一些技术解决方案在实验室环境中表现出色，但在实际应用中，如果这些技术增加了医生日常工作的复杂性，或者无法与医院的现有系统无缝对接，就会导致其难以被广泛采纳。这一现象反映出医疗技术采纳的一个重要障碍，即临床工作流程的缺口。文章强调，解决实际问题并在日常工作中产生积极影响，是推动医疗技术成功应用的关键。

在医疗行业，医生的工作流程通常是高度复杂且繁忙的，任何可能导致额外负担的技术都可能被抵制。因此，医疗技术的设计和实施必须充分考虑临床工作流程的实际需求，确保技术能够与现有系统有效整合，以减少对医生工作的干扰。作者呼吁研发团队在技术开发阶段就应与临床医生密切合作，了解他们的需求和痛点，从而设计出更符合实际使用场景的解决方案。

此外，文章还指出，成功的医疗技术不仅需要在技术层面上具备先进性，更需要在实际应用中展现出其对临床工作的积极影响。只有当医疗技术能够真正解决临床医生面临的实际问题，并在日常工作中提供便利时，才能获得医生的认可和采纳。因此，推动医疗技术的成功应用，关键在于如何有效地缩小技术与临床工作流程之间的差距，确保技术的实用性和可操作性。

items.title: Nanotechnology-driven optogenetics for therapeutic grade interventions.
items.body: Optogenetics, a biotechnology that combines optical and genetic strategies to regulate cellular and tissue functions with high spatial and temporal precision, serves as a powerful tool-level regulatory technology widely employed to investigate cellular processes and elucidate disease mechanisms. Nanotechnology-driven optogenetics, which incorporates nanomaterials/nanostructures to improve the efficacy and broaden the applications of optogenetic systems, synergistically integrates the precision, tunability, and multifunctionality of nanotechnology with the spatiotemporal control inherent to optogenetics. The development not only enhances the flexibility and efficiency of optogenetic technology but also advances the field toward therapeutic-grade interventions. In this review, we summarize recent advances in nanotechnology-driven optogenetics, with a particular emphasis on three key areas: (1) nanostructured light sources for the precise activation of optogenetic systems, which include both externally light-stimulated systems and systems that operate independently of external light sources; (2) nanotechnology-enabled targeted delivery of light-sensitive proteins and genetic constructs to ensure efficient modulation of optogenetic pathways, which specifically involves the nanotechnology-assisted gene, protein, and recombinase enzyme delivery approaches; and (3) nanotechnology-driven therapeutic applications of optogenetics, including CAR T cell immunotherapy, cancer treatment, neurological interventions, and cardiac therapies. We further discuss the current challenges facing this emerging field and outline future research directions. This review aims not only to highlight recent breakthroughs but also to position nanotechnology-driven optogenetics as a promising tool for next-generation precision medicine.
items.authors: Chen X, Zhang X, Zhao Y.
items.title_zh: 纳米技术驱动的光遗传学在治疗干预中的应用
items.summary_zh: 光遗传学是一种结合光学和遗传策略以高空间和时间精度调控细胞及组织功能的生物技术，广泛用于研究细胞过程和阐明疾病机制。纳米技术驱动的光遗传学通过引入纳米材料/纳米结构，提升了光遗传系统的有效性并扩展了其应用范围，结合了纳米技术的精确性、可调性和多功能性与光遗传学固有的时空控制。本文综述了纳米技术驱动的光遗传学的最新进展，重点关注三个关键领域：（1）用于精确激活光遗传系统的纳米结构光源，包括外部光刺激系统和独立于外部光源的系统；（2）纳米技术促进的光敏蛋白和基因构建体的靶向递送，以确保高效调控光遗传通路；（3）纳米技术驱动的其他相关应用。
items.l1_lead: 纳米技术的引入显著提升了光遗传学的有效性和应用范围，为细胞功能调控和疾病机制研究提供了更精确的工具和方法。
items.l2_summary:
光遗传学是一种结合光学和遗传策略的生物技术，能够以高空间和时间精度调控细胞及组织功能，广泛应用于细胞过程研究和疾病机制阐明。近年来，纳米技术的引入为光遗传学的发展带来了新的机遇，提升了光遗传系统的有效性并扩展了其应用范围。纳米技术驱动的光遗传学结合了纳米材料和纳米结构的精确性、可调性与多功能性，进一步增强了光遗传学的时空控制能力。

在这一领域的最新进展中，研究者们重点关注了三个关键领域。首先，纳米结构光源的开发使得光遗传系统的激活更加精确。这些光源包括外部光刺激系统和独立于外部光源的系统，能够在不同的实验条件下提供灵活的光照方案，从而实现对细胞功能的精准调控。其次，纳米技术在光敏蛋白和基因构建体的靶向递送方面也发挥了重要作用。通过纳米载体，研究者能够确保光敏蛋白和基因构建体高效地递送到目标细胞，从而有效调控光遗传通路，提升实验的成功率和可靠性。最后，纳米技术驱动的光遗传学还在其他相关应用中展现出广阔的前景，推动了生物医学领域的创新。

综上所述，纳米技术驱动的光遗传学不仅提升了光遗传系统的性能，还为细胞功能的调控提供了新的思路和方法。随着纳米技术的不断发展，未来在疾病治疗和基础生物研究中，光遗传学的应用将更加广泛和深入。

items.title: Are you going to make that green light? A new, Kitchener-made traffic light technology has the answer - CBC
items.body:

For them to know in advance if they're going to make a signal or not, this can be life or death.” / “Knowing when to stop allows vehicles to save on fuel consumption, because they have more information on when to slow down for a traffic light.” / “This is basically the reverse data flow. Instead of into the signal, it's from the signal back to the driver to influence the vehicle.”

(Lauren Kuivenhoven/CBC) Social Sharing If you've ever found yourself second guessing whether you should speed up to make a green light, a new traffic light technology in Kitchener may help.
Kitchener-based company Miovision, a global intelligence transportation system vendor, launched vehicle to everything (V2X) in the city a few months ago.
It's a technology that connects traffic light information to cars, and lets drivers know when a light is going to be red or green by displaying a traffic light icon on the vehicle’s dashboard.
“Knowing what the signal is doing reduces your stress level dramatically … I know I don't need to rush because it's not going to do me any good,” said Thomas Bauer, the vice president of V2X at Miovision.
Thomas Bauer, the vice president of V2X at Miovision, explains how information from traffic lights is connected to cars. (Lauren Kuivenhoven/CBC) The traffic icon provides a countdown to green, the speed a driver must stay at to make a green light and a warning about when the light will turn red. Bauer says if a driver is going over the speed limit, the display will disappear.
The countdown to a green light will disappear four seconds before the light changes, “just to make sure that you are now looking out the window,” said Bauer.
He says the technology is meant as a driving assist for now, although it's a stepping stone toward autonomous driving.
Bauer says the technology offers both safety and environmental benefits. He says it’s especially valuable for heavy vehicles.
“They have a much longer braking distance. For them to know in advance if they're going to make a signal or not, this can be life or death.”
Bauer says knowing when to stop allows vehicles to save on fuel consumption, because they have more information on when to slow down for a traffic light.
Miovision started out by counting cars to help with transportation planning, and expanded to emergency vehicle pre-emption, which modifies the traffic signal to allow emergency vehicle or public transit through an intersection.
Miovision's V2X technology provides a countdown to a green light on a vehicle's dashboard. (Lauren Kuivenhoven/CBC) Now the company has launched V2X in Kitchener, which allows data from traffic lights to flow into vehicles over a cellular network.
“Kitchener is one of these cities in Canada where we have most of our equipment deployed. It's now available, I would say about 90 per cent of the intersections here,” said Bauer.
According to the Region of Waterloo, Miovision technology has been connected to traffic lights across the region since 2020.
In an emailed statement to CBC News, the region says the system uses cameras and other detection devices that are connected to the traffic signal controller.
Data is retrieved about cyclists, pedestrians and vehicles to "optimize the operation of the traffic signals,” said the statement, in part.
Kitchener-made tech connects cars to traffic light grid
September 1 | Duration closed caption 4:22 Miovision launched V2X in Kitchener a few months ago, a technology that connects traffic light information to cars. It lets drivers know when the light will turn red or green. Thomas Bauer, the vice president of V2X at Miovision, showed CBC K-W's Lauren Kuivenhoven how the technology works. With the new V2X technology, Bauer says instead of just collecting data about cars and intersections, the cars will be able to also receive data from the traffic lights.
"This is basically the reverse data flow. Instead of into the signal, it's from the signal back to the driver to influence the vehicle," said Bauer.
V2X currently covers more than 70,000 intersections across eight countries.
It’s available in VW Group cars, such as Audi, Bently and Porsche. Bauer says drivers can also download an app to connect the technology to their car, if they don't have a car brand from VW Group.
