items.article_body:
Facebook LinkedIn Email Print Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Artistic Director Robin Murray, Cultural Park Theatre Actor reads monologue for casting director at Cultural Park Theatre. Whether auditioning for a comedy, drama or musical, an actor arrives at an audition equipped with a head shot, resume and a couple of monologues. Cultural Park Theatre Executive Director Robin Murray says the monologue plays a crucial role in her decision about whether or not to use an actor in a show she is casting.
“I consider a monologue the first handshake that you're giving a director,” said Murray. “It kind of shows what your abilities are without having somebody to rely on, another castmate to rely on or a set or a prop. And we can see what your range is, if you are able to move your body and your voice along with the words without relying on other things on a set.”
According to Murray, the best monologues don’t just showcase an actor’s talent and versatility, they tell a story with a beginning, middle and end.
“I like to see like the seasons in a monologue when somebody gives it,” Murray added. “I want to see them start as them and then I want to see an arc and then I want to see almost a resolution and then an ending.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actor, author, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues for kids. Local actor, director and theatre instructor Gerrie Benzing has just published a new book of monologues. She knows exactly what casting directors such as Murray want.
“Since a monologue is a chance to show a director what you can do. I try to put more than one emotion in any monologue I write, so that there's a bit of an arc in it, so that you can show you can play different emotions,” Benzing said.
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing in the role of Lee in Charles Busch's 'The Tale of the Allergist's Wife.' Benzing’s experiences auditioning for roles, performing in a wide variety of shows and teaching theater to children and teens informs the way she crafts each monologue. But it was happenstance that led her to publish three compilations of the monologues she’s been writing since 2006.
“My monologue started, of course, with my own son, who was performing at the time, and we could not find a monologue anywhere that was different, that was new,” Benzing explained. “So, I wrote him one. And he entered the Young Artist Competition, and he was only 10. And it was a competition that went all the way up to college. And he won the whole thing. And so, everybody said please write me a monologue.”
Since then, actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Actors using her monologues have enjoyed considerable success winning roles and competitions around the globe. “I have had a student text me from South Africa. He entered a worldwide monologue competition and he won his category. He's since been cast in all kinds of films,” Benzing noted. “I had a boy who auditioned for a Broadway show and used one of my monologues and he was cast. But my biggest success story was Michael Fatica, who I started teaching in summer camps here at the Cultural Park. And he has become a successful star on Broadway.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing It’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings. But it’s everyday kids having success on a local level that really touches Benzing’s heartstrings.
“The thing that makes me the most proud are the kids that text me and say, ‘Hey, I won my student talent show.’ ‘I got second place. I almost won.’” Benzing added. “And they are so happy. And the fact that I could give them something that they love to do and that they did well with and they were happy with, I think that's the thing that makes me the most happy.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing will sign copies of 'Character Monologues for Kids' following the 7:30 p.m. performance of 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory' on September 19. Cultural Park Theatre will be hosting a book signing for Benzing’s latest book, “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment,” following the 7 p.m. performance of “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory” on Sept. 19 .
The event marks a milestone in Benzing’s career as an author.
“This is my absolute first one and I’m super excited about it.” Benzing noted.
A Chicago native, Robin Murray caught the acting bug in fourth grade. Now living in Southwest Florida, Murray is the producing artistic director of Cultural Park Theatre.
“Cultural Park Theatre is one of the longest running community theaters in Lee County,” Murray noted. “We are now entering into our 64th season. We produce adult plays, children’s plays, comedies, dramas, rom-cons and musicals as well. And our musicals are usually on the lighter side and include children.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre. Actors use sides during an audition at Cultural Park Theatre. Every theater has its own way of announcing auditions.
“At Cultural Park, we put out a call usually on social media and then we will give the breakdown of what each character is and whether or not you need to come in with a 16-bar song, 60 seconds, 90 seconds,” Murray said. “For our regular plays, we will also have the breakdown and we will ask you either to come in with a monologue, be very familiar with the show, and then we will have you read sides.”
The term “sides” refers to excerpts from the script that actors are given to learn for an audition. This excerpt could be an entire scene, or just part of one. Depending on the project, sides can also include more than one section of the script for an actor to learn.
The term dates back to Shakespeare, when actors were only given their lines for rehearsals since scripts had to be written longhand.
Theaters often provide the sides in advance of the audition so that actors can familiarize themselves with the lines prior to arriving.
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre The purpose of a well-chosen monologue is to demonstrate an actor's versatility. While a side will give the casting director a rough idea about how an actor will potentially handle the role they’re auditioning for and fit in with the rest of the cast, sides do not reflect the actor’s overall skill set. That’s the purpose of a well-chosen monologue, Murray said.
“Based on the monologue, we know whether or not you're versatile, and that's the biggest thing we need in an actor, to be versatile,” Murray said. The monologue is going to show us an actor’s range where the sides are going to show us if they can carry a character, the specific character.”
Courtesy of Cultural Park Theatre / Robin Murray, Artistic Director, Cultural Park Theatre To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch from drama to comedy while reading a monologue. To gauge an actor’s versatility, the casting director will often have ask the auditioner to switch up the tenor of the reading.
“If you are saying a line that’s very comedic, the director might ask you to read it in a more serious tone,” Murray pointed out.
While monologues are important in all genres, Murray noted that for musical auditions, “the voice is weighted the most because, depending on the part the person is auditioning for, if they cannot hit the note ….”
In addition to directing, Murray is an accomplished actor. Her stage credits include the evil nurse Pat Jones in “Four Old Broads” for The Belle Theatre and Mary Jane McMann in “Inspecting Carol.” She also appeared in “Marvin’s Room,” “I Remember Mama,” “Anton in Show Business,” “The Last Days of Judas Iscariot,” “Picasso at the Lapin Agile,” “On Golden Pond,” “Five Kinds of Silence” and “Calendar Girls.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Benzing played the part of Ruth in the Naples Players' production of 'Calendar Girls' in 2021. About Gerrie Benzing
As the creative director of Monologues4kids.com, Gerrie Benzing has written numerous children’s plays and over 500 monologues for clients worldwide. Dozens of children have used Benzing’s monologues to win movie roles, theater auditions, talent shows and pageants and to secure professional representation.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing Gerrie Benzing's new book 'Character Monologues for Kids.' Her new book is “Character Monologues for Kids: Own the Moment.”
“I have a lot of monologues,” noted Benzing, who has been writing monologues for more than 20 years. “A lot of them are straight comedic monologues, but many are character monologues as well, like Goldilocks talking about how she's not a criminal. When I directed kid shows, I loved seeing characters in the monologue selection. So that's what this [latest book] is, a book of character monologues.”
She included nearly 100 for “Character Monologues for Kids.”
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Kids' is among Benzing's books of monologues. Her previous books are “Duet Acting Scenes for Teens,” “Duet Acting Scenes for Kids,” “Monologues4kids Theater Camp Plays: Broadway Version” and “Commercials for Kids.” She has also contributed original monologues to the book “Active Listening,” by Michael Rost and J.J. Wilson.
Courtesy of Gerrie Benzing / Gerrie Benzing 'Duet Acting Scenes for Teens' is among Benzing's books of monologues. “I have lots more monologues,” Benzing added. “So there are more books coming. Lots of them.”
A local stage and film actor, director and musical theatre instructor, Benzing has directed six mainstage productions at Cultural Park Theater, including “Chicago” (2019), “Sister Act” in 2018 (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award), “Boeing, Boeing” in 2016 (for which she won as Cultural Park Theatre Best Director Marquee Award) and “Peter Pan” (for which she garnered a Cultural Park Best Director of a Musical Marquee Award in 2014).
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Ethel Thayer in 'On Golden Pond' at Cultural Park Theatre in 2019 She has also appeared in more than a dozen shows at Cultural Park Theatre, including the iconic role of Ethel Thayer in “On Golden Pond,” “Harvey” (for which she won a Cultural Park Theatre Best Actress Marquee Award for her portrayal of Veta), “The Glass Menagerie” (in which she was cast as Amanda), “Dixie Swim Club” (Sharee), Bella Manningham in “Angel Street” (Gaslight) , “Bad Seed” (Christine) and Jack Neary’s “The Porch.”
“We asked Gerrie to do a book signing following Saturday night’s performance of ‘Charlie and the Chocolate Factory’ because she’s been an important staple here at the theater,” Murray noted. “A lot of the kids that are directing shows and working here have worked with Gerrie since they were 5 years old. So, it just is a natural thing to bring her back and have her showcase those monologues that the kids use to start their careers.”
WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall / WGCU Arts Reporter Tom Hall Gerrie Benzing as Frau Blucher in The Belle Theatre's 2025 production of 'Young Frankenstein.' Benzing’s other stage credits include Frau Blucher in “Young Frankenstein” at The Belle Theatre, a Pigeon sister in “The Odd Couple” at Fort Myers Theatre, swing for Mary Meeker in “Unnecessary Farce” at Off Broadway Palm, cigarette-smoking, whiskey-swilling sexpot Elaine Navazio in Neil Simon’s “Last of the Red Hot Lovers” for The Belle Theatre, Julia Budder in “It’s Only a Play” at The Studio Players, Caprice in “A Doublewide, Texas Christmas” at Broadway Palm Dinner Theatre, Mother Superior in “Drinking Habits” (The Belle Theatre), Gertrude in “Save Hamlet” (for Lab Theater), Raven in “Trouble (at the Vista View Mobile Home Estates)” for Florida Rep
items.title_zh: 独白：演员展示多样性的关键
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了独白在演员试镜中的重要性。科学家指出，独白是演员与导演之间的首次接触，能够展示演员的多样性和能力。通过独白，导演可以判断演员是否具备多变的表演能力，这是演员最需要的特质。文章强调，独白不仅展示了演员的情感范围，还能体现他们的表演技巧，而侧面剧本则只能反映演员对特定角色的理解。因此，独白在试镜中起着至关重要的作用，能够帮助导演评估演员的潜力和适应性。
items.l1_lead: 独白在演员试镜中至关重要，它不仅展示了演员的多样性和情感范围，还能帮助导演评估其表演能力和适应性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了独白（monologue）在演员试镜中的重要性，强调其在演员与导演之间首次接触时所发挥的关键作用。科学家指出，独白不仅是演员展示自身多样性和表演能力的机会，也是导演评估演员是否具备多变表演能力的重要依据。这种多变性被认为是演员最需要的特质之一。通过独白，演员能够展现出丰富的情感范围和高超的表演技巧，而侧面剧本（side script）则往往只能反映演员对特定角色的理解，无法全面展示其表演潜力。

文章进一步强调，独白在试镜中的重要性体现在其能够帮助导演更全面地评估演员的适应性和潜力。通过独白，导演可以观察到演员在不同情境下的表现，进而判断其是否适合某个角色。这种评估不仅依赖于演员的情感表达，还包括他们对角色的诠释能力和即兴发挥的能力。因此，独白在演员试镜中扮演着至关重要的角色，是导演选择合适演员的重要依据。

总的来说，独白作为一种表演形式，不仅展示了演员的个人魅力和专业素养，还为导演提供了一个全面评估演员能力的平台。这使得独白在试镜过程中不可或缺，成为演员与导演之间沟通和理解的桥梁。

items.title: Introducing Biomni: Stanford’s AI co-scientist built to accelerate biomedical research - The Brighter Side of News
items.body:
原话：“If you think of an agent as a carpenter, a carpenter without tools is just a carpenter who can talk.” / “The hurdle in biomedical science is not intelligence or ideas; it is mechanics.” / “This difference is not just about efficiency. It changes how research can be done.”
论点：Biomni可以在几分钟内完成传统上需要人类60小时的工作，从而加速生物医学研究的进展。
论据：在40分钟内，Biomni清理了数据，结合了数据，创建了可视化，并识别了饮食与体温之间的联系。
items.authors: Jure Leskovec
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（The Brighter Side of News） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: If you think of an agent as a carpenter, a carpenter without tools is just a carpenter who can talk.
The hurdle in biomedical science is not intelligence or ideas; it is mechanics.
This difference is not just about efficiency. It changes how research can be done.
items.topic_zh: Biomni在生物医学研究中的作用
items.claim_zh: Biomni可以在几分钟内完成传统上需要人类60小时的工作，从而加速生物医学研究的进展。
items.evidence_zh: 在40分钟内，Biomni清理了数据，结合了数据，创建了可视化，并识别了饮食与体温之间的联系。
items.article_body:
A new AI system called Biomni can design experiments, analyze data, and accelerate biomedical research in minutes. (CREDIT: Shutterstock)
Stanford University researchers developed Biomni, an AI “co-scientist” that can read scientific papers, analyze datasets, write and execute code, form hypotheses, and design experiments in minutes. Biomni uses 150 specialized tools, 105 software packages, and 59 databases across 25 areas of biology, allowing it to complete complex biomedical research tasks at speeds far beyond traditional human workflows. Researchers say Biomni is designed to augment rather than replace scientists, handling labor-intensive research tasks while leaving interpretation, creativity, and final decision-making to humans.
A new kind of scientific partner is beginning to take shape in research labs. It does not wear a lab coat or hold a pipette. Instead, it reads thousands of papers, writes code, analyzes data, and suggests new experiments in minutes. Researchers at Stanford University call it Biomni, an artificial intelligence system designed to act as a “co-scientist.”
The system, described in the journal Science , reflects a growing effort to rethink how research is done. As scientific knowledge expands, the challenge is no longer just having ideas. It is managing the enormous workload required to test them.
“If you think of an agent as a carpenter, a carpenter without tools is just a carpenter who can talk,” said Jure Leskovec, professor of computer science at Stanford. “With Biomni, we give the carpenter a set of tools, so it can build.”
Modern biomedical research moves at a fast pace. New studies appear daily, and datasets grow larger each year. Yet progress often slows under the weight of routine tasks.
Scientists must read literature, organize data, write code, and test ideas before reaching conclusions. Each step takes time. Together, they can delay discovery for weeks or months.
“The hurdle in biomedical science is not intelligence or ideas; it is mechanics,” Leskovec said. “It’s this laborious stuff that slows innovation. Biomni can do this work in minutes.”
This challenge has created a gap between what researchers know and what they can act on. Important patterns may remain hidden simply because there is not enough time to explore them.
Biomni was designed to close that gap. The idea is simple. A scientist should be able to ask a question in plain language and receive a complete research workflow in return.
The system reads scientific papers, forms hypotheses , selects datasets, and chooses the right tools. It writes and runs code, interprets results, and suggests next steps.
“Biomni is able to understand a simple question like, ‘Why are these patients responding differently to the drug?’” said Kexin Huang, who helped lead the project. “Then it digs in, doing a lot of the scientific legwork.”
This process turns a single question into a structured investigation. Instead of handling one task at a time, the system manages the entire pipeline from start to finish.
To achieve this, researchers built a large digital environment for the system. Biomni draws on full-text papers, code repositories, and datasets from across the biomedical field.
It includes 150 specialized tools, 105 software packages, and 59 databases. These resources span 25 areas of biology, from genetics to neuroscience.
The system identifies which tools are needed for a given task. It then combines them into a step-by-step plan. Each step is translated into code that can be executed automatically.
This design allows Biomni to adapt to many types of problems. It does not rely on a fixed workflow . Instead, it builds a new one for each question.
The system’s speed is one of its most striking features. In one real-world example, a researcher uploaded more than 450 files of health data. These included glucose levels, food intake, and physical activity.
The user asked a simple question. Analyze the data and find meaningful patterns.
Within 40 minutes, Biomni cleaned the data, combined it, created visualizations , and identified links between diet and body temperature. Leskovec said the same work could take a human more than 60 hours.
This difference is not just about efficiency. It changes how research can be done. Faster analysis allows scientists to test more ideas and explore more possibilities.
To evaluate performance, researchers tested Biomni on hundreds of biomedical questions. These included tasks such as gene identification and disease analysis.
The system performed well across these areas. In many cases, it matched the accuracy of experienced researchers. It also completed tasks much faster.
In one test involving rare disease diagnosis , Biomni reached 60 percent accuracy. This was similar to experts, who scored between 60 and 70 percent. However, the system finished the task in three minutes, while humans took nearly two hours.
In another test focused on gene detection, it achieved 80 percent accuracy. It reduced analysis time from about 90 minutes to just four minutes.
These results suggest that the system can support experts by handling time-consuming work.
Biomni does more than analyze data. It can also design experiments and guide laboratory work.
In one case, the system generated a complete protocol for DNA cloning . It included detailed steps, materials, and validation methods.
Researchers followed the instructions in the lab. The experiment worked as expected. Colonies grew, and DNA sequencing confirmed the results.
This ability to connect digital analysis with physical experiments is a key strength. It shows that the system can move from theory to practice.
Another advantage lies in how Biomni tracks its work. Every step is recorded and linked to sources.
The system provides full citations for the data and methods it uses. This allows researchers to verify results and reproduce findings.
In science, reproducibility is essential. By documenting its process, Biomni helps strengthen the reliability of research.
Despite its capabilities, researchers stress that Biomni is not meant to replace scientists.
The system can process information quickly and find patterns. However, it does not make final decisions. Human judgment remains central to the scientific process.
“And it always will,” Huang said. “This is not about machines taking over science, but more about machines becoming a powerful new partner to augment human researchers.”
The goal is to free scientists from routine tasks. This allows them to focus on creativity, interpretation, and decision-making .
The system still has limits. It does not cover every area of biology. Some tasks require more detailed input to ensure accuracy.
Researchers are working to expand its capabilities. Future versions may include more data sources and improved reasoning methods.
There are also questions about safety. Tools that can design experiments must be used responsibly. Developers emphasize the importance of transparency and ethical guidelines .
Even with these challenges, early adoption is strong. More than 10,000 labs have begun using the system in academic and industry settings.
The rise of systems like Biomni reflects a broader shift in research. As knowledge grows, collaboration between humans and machines becomes more important.
Instead of working alone, scientists may rely on digital partners that handle complex workflows . This could speed up discovery and open new paths for innovation.
For fields like medicine, the impact could be profound. Faster research may lead to quicker development of treatments and deeper understanding of disease.
This work could transform how biomedical research is conducted. By automating routine tasks, it allows scientists to focus on deeper questions and creative thinking. This may accelerate discoveries in areas such as drug development and disease prevention.
The system also lowers barriers to entry. Researchers with fewer resources can access advanced tools and perform complex analyses. This could expand participation in science and increase global collaboration.
In healthcare, faster data analysis may improve patient outcomes. Researchers can identify patterns more quickly and develop targeted treatments. Over time, this may lead to more personalized medicine.
For the scientific community, improved transparency and reproducibility strengthen trust in research. By documenting every step, the system helps ensure that findings can be verified and built upon.
Research findings are available online in the journal Science .
The original story " Introducing Biomni: Stanford’s AI co-scientist built to accelerate biomedical research " is published in The Brighter Side of News.

items.title: Tributes paid to Jason Arday after former Cambridge professor’s death - The Guardian
items.body:
原话：“At the heart of all of this was a man who’d been diagnosed in childhood with disabilities that included autism and language delay and learning differences.” / “He was a vulnerable child, a vulnerable teenager and a vulnerable adult, so he needed and deserved safeguarding and support and reasonable adjustment every step of the way.”
论点：阿尔代在成长过程中作为一个脆弱的个体，应该得到每一步的保护和支持。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen

items.claim_zh: 阿尔代在成长过程中作为一个脆弱的个体，应该得到每一步的保护和支持。
items.article_body:
Jason Arday was found dead at his home in south London on Friday. Photograph: Christian Sinibaldi/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Jason Arday was found dead at his home in south London on Friday. Photograph: Christian Sinibaldi/The Guardian Jason Arday This article is more than 1 month old Tributes paid to Jason Arday after former Cambridge professor’s death This article is more than 1 month old Andy Burnham calls for reflection after ‘tragedy on so many levels’ in comments echoed by London mayor Sadiq Khan
Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham has called the death of Jason Arday , whose body was found at his home in south London on Friday, a “tragedy on so many levels”.
Arday resigned as a professor at the University of Cambridge last week after allegations of plagiarism, which he denied. He was pronounced dead just after 3pm on Friday .
In a statement issued via his publisher, Simon & Schuster UK, the former academic’s family said they were “in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son”.
Speaking to broadcasters during a visit to Cornwall on Saturday, the prime minister said: “It’s a tragedy on so many levels, but particularly just for everybody who knew Jason, his family obviously, his friends. We think of them today.
“It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this. A really sad, sad and sorry state of affairs and I think we all today think of Jason, his contribution and his family and friends.”
More than £20,000 has been raised for the family of Arday after the Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon launched a fundraising drive via GoFundMe in his memory.
Other leading figures to pay tribute included the London mayor, Sadiq Khan, and the Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy.
Khan said: “I’m devastated for the family and friends of Jason Arday. He faced an unacceptable public hounding and campaign of abuse. I know many Londoners will be angry and upset this evening.
“Jason Arday was the victim of a pernicious public shaming that other people in his position simply wouldn’t have faced. His death was a tragedy, but once again it should be a wake-up call for all of us.”
Speaking on Newsnight, Ribeiro-Addy read out a list of names including William O’Reilly, Ros Holmes, David Latchman, and Nicola Morrison. “These are all people that have actually proven to have been plagiarists, or people that have manipulated their data, and people that have been proven to have lifted whole pages from students’ papers or published work that they had to withdraw,” she said.
Ribeiro-Addy said there had been a media witch-hunt which was cruel because “it didn’t aim to just target him”.
“It aimed to target anybody that supported him, trying to isolate him as much as possible, going after people who had signed up to statements,” she said. “The difference between them and him was they were white, and he was not.”
The Conservative MP James Cleverly expressed his anger over Arday’s death. In a statement on X, he wrote that a number of people at academic institutions “have serious questions to answer”.
“They put him into positions he was clearly not qualified for so they could have a black wunderkind to show off, they pushed him into the spotlight for their own benefit,” they said. “His exposure was inevitable, a case of when, not if. His whole world fell apart.”
Simon Baron-Cohen, a clinical psychologist and the director of the Autism Research Centre, who was a friend of Arday’s, told Radio 4’s Today programme that he contacted him Friday morning and said that he felt he was unable to go on.
“He used those words in voice notes,” Baron-Cohen said. “At the heart of all of this was a man who’d been diagnosed in childhood with disabilities that included autism and language delay and learning differences.
“He was a vulnerable child, a vulnerable teenager and a vulnerable adult, so he needed and deserved safeguarding and support and reasonable adjustment every step of the way.”

Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters
Arday was initially accused of plagiarising another person’s work in his PhD thesis, but denied all allegations. A review conducted by Liverpool John Moores University, where he completed his doctorate, upheld its decision to award him a PhD earlier this year.
In recent weeks, other elements of his life story were increasingly questioned , including claims of prodigious money-raising for charity and feats of long-distance running. He was also challenged about whether he was nonverbal as a child.
The National Education Union general secretary, Daniel Kebede, said Arday had been subjected to “a public and brutal takedown that unleashed a tirade of racism”.
“I don’t believe this was ever simply about ‘professional conduct’ or ‘plagiarism’,” he said.
“There is a profound difference between scrutiny and a sustained public campaign that turns an individual into a symbol of everything the right believes is wrong with DEI.
“The effect has been chilling. It tells Black people and others from underrepresented backgrounds that entering prominent public positions will make you a target.
“A target not only for criticism of your work, but for a much broader political and cultural backlash.”
The Metropolitan police said his death was being treated as unexpected, but not believed to be suspicious.
In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org . In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org
This article was amended on 16 August 2026 to correct the spelling of the names of Ros Holmes and David Latchman.

items.summary_zh: 文章讨论了已故剑桥大学教授阿尔代的成长经历，强调他在童年时期被诊断出自闭症、语言延迟和学习差异等障碍。作者指出，阿尔代作为一个脆弱的孩子、青少年和成年人，始终需要并应当得到保护、支持和合理的调整。文章的核心论点是，社会应为像阿尔代这样的脆弱个体提供必要的保障，以确保他们在成长过程中能够获得平等的机会和支持。

items.l2_summary:
阿尔代（Alday）是已故剑桥大学教授，他的成长经历为我们提供了对脆弱个体保护与支持的重要思考。文章指出，阿尔代在童年时期被诊断出自闭症（Autism）、语言延迟（Language Delay）和学习差异（Learning Differences），这些障碍使他在生活的各个阶段都面临着挑战。作为一个脆弱的孩子、青少年和成年人，阿尔代始终需要保护和支持，这不仅是他个人的需求，也是社会应承担的责任。

文章的核心论点强调，社会应为像阿尔代这样的脆弱个体提供必要的保障，以确保他们在成长过程中能够获得平等的机会和支持。阿尔代的经历表明，缺乏适当的支持和合理的调整，脆弱个体可能会面临更大的困难和孤立。因此，社会各界应当关注这些个体的需求，提供必要的资源和环境，以帮助他们克服障碍，实现自我价值。

通过对阿尔代的成长故事的分析，作者呼吁社会重视脆弱个体的权益，倡导建立一个包容的环境，使每一个人都能在平等的基础上获得发展机会。这样的支持不仅有助于脆弱个体的成长，也将促进整个社会的和谐与进步。总之，阿尔代的经历提醒我们，保护和支持脆弱个体是社会的共同责任，只有通过集体的努力，才能为他们创造一个更加友好的生活和学习环境。

Derek Owusu: ‘I’ve never figured out how to live in the world’
Two weeks ago, following a conversation with Jason Arday, Professor Simon Baron-Cohen posted a message on X.
The psychologist said he was “very concerned” about the impact of media coverage on his friend, who had autism, and linked it to work his Autism Research Centre at Cambridge University had done showing that autistic people were at a greater risk of suicide.
“This is relentless bullying of a vulnerable autistic man and raises safe-guarding issues,” he wrote. “It’s time to stop.” The site’s owner, Elon Musk, responded to the post with one word: “Liar”.
Yesterday, Baron-Cohen said Arday had sent him a voice note via WhatsApp on the morning of his death. “He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life, and he wasn’t coping with… he felt he couldn’t go on,” he told Radio 4’s Today programme.
In 2022, Baron-Cohen and psychologists from other UK universities found that autistic people had an elevated risk of suicide. They examined 372 coroners’ inquest reports over a three-year period to find out whether the person who died had been diagnosed with autism or had autistic traits. They found evidence of autism in more than 10% of those who died, compared with about 1.1% of the population overall.
Jill Aylott, founder of the National Autism and ADHD Assessment Centre, said: “accountability should never require us to abandon humanity.
“When somebody becomes the focus of sustained national criticism, particularly where that person is known to be neurodivergent, institutions should be asking: who is checking that this person is safe?”
Baron-Cohen said that for the last 10 days he had seen Arday’s mental health “getting worse and worse”.
George Brown: the former Post Office boy who unlocked the mystery of depression
Derek Owusu: ‘I’ve never figured out how to live in the world’
“We need to let the investigations proceed. We need to understand how this tragedy has happened, but there has to be accountability at lots of levels.”

items.title: Escaping The Bunker: Bobby Gillespie On Primal Scream’s Most Uncompromising Era - clashmusic.com
items.body:
原话：“I think people like myself have been in opposition all our lives.” / “We just followed our hearts. We weren’t in competition with any other band.” / “I’m trying to write the newest Primal Scream song.”
论点：他认为Primal Scream的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛，强调追随内心而非竞争。
论据：他提到自己和乐队在创作时不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达。

items.topic_zh: 音乐创作与反叛精神
items.claim_zh: 他认为Primal Scream的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛，强调追随内心而非竞争。

items.article_body:
Bobby Gillespie is a raconteur. A true punk, the Glasgow-born frontman has led Primal Scream through multiple iterations and evolutions, refusing to be hemmed in by expectations. For some fans, their peak came as the debauchery of the 90s collapsed into the paranoia of the Millennium, with a triptych of albums – ‘Vanishing Point’, ‘XTRMNTR’ and ‘Evil Heat’ – presenting the group at their most sonically and politically uncompromising.
Now, he’s taking a rare glimpse back. Spruced up for a lavish re-issue project and an accompanying nationwide tour, ‘The Bunker Trilogy’ – as band mate Andrew Innes terms this period – remains a bracing, inspired listen, a fusion of post-punk, jazz, club culture electronics, and revolutionary politics.
“The idea was: no rules,” he tells CLASH. “Those albums were all recorded in a particular way. We deconstructed the band after ‘Give Out But Don’t Give Up’ – we lost some members. Robert Young, the guitarist, stepped back, so we began to stop writing songs based around guitar riffs, and started writing songs based around rhythm and atmosphere and texture.”
“Andrew Innes and I would go into the studio five days a week. On ‘Give Out But Don’t Give Up’ we reverted to a traditional band structure, but with The Bunker Trilogy that was cast to the wind.”
The highlights rank not only with the band’s best work, but challenge any other group working in that time period. Songs like ‘Star’ and ‘Kowalski’ took daring musicianship and production into the charts, built from the ground up in their tiny London studio. “I had things I wanted to express that I couldn’t express before because I was too inarticulate with language, and maybe too inarticulate with sound and song structure,” Bobby explains, “but the experience that we gathered, meant that we were in a position where we could actually finally make a statement that we’d always wanted to make.”
“We were able to realise something we’d always dreamed of doing by that point because we had the know-how, the expertise, the knowledge, the confidence, and the attitude.”
It helps that the guest cast contains some of British music’s most potent names. my bloody valentine maestro Kevin Shields joins for ‘XTRMNTR’, while the collapse of Manchester icons The Stone Roses saw bass player Mani join the group for a decade-long stint.
“Mani was a great bassist, a great musician,” the frontman notes. “But he was also this life-affirming, fun-love character. And he was very, very smart. He was a Grammar School boy – he went to the same Grammar School as Anthony Burgess, the guy that wrote A Clockwork Orange.” “Underneath that cheeky chappie Manc persona, Mani was a very smart guy. And we had so much fun, so many laughs… and he never played a bad gig.”
If the Bunker title is slightly tongue in cheek, it also reflects the band’s oppositional stance to British music at the time – the Britpop party was fading, stubbed out cigarettes were floating in glasses of flat champagne, and New Labour was firmly in power. “I think people like myself have been in opposition all our lives,” he says. “It was always this us and them attitude. That’s why we were punks when we were teenagers. We needed punk to articulate that, so we could realise we weren’t alone.”
“Britpop was very conservative music, so Primal Scream were definitely not part of that,” he says. “We just followed our hearts. We weren’t in competition with any other band.”
“We just had a different approach to every other band at the time,” he notes. “They were still writing and recording and producing records in the traditional manner that old rock groups did, but we deconstructed that and took a different approach.”
‘XTRMNTR’ lead single ‘Swastika Eyes’ wasn’t built for Radio 1 plays, as Bobby points out. “Radio stations weren’t going to play that song. We were being uncompromising, but that’s how we felt. It was what we wrote about, and if it’s unpalatable for daytime radio then so be it.”
“I kind of felt that at the end of the 90s you’d seen American bombers taking off from British airfields – because we’re kind of like an occupied country, aren’t we? We’re an aircraft carrier for the United States. The whole thing for me was, I think they’re gearing up for something bigger. This is just a dry run for something bigger.”
“And yes, that’s a dystopian view of the world, but I think it just came from the literature I was reading at the time, which was very paranoid. But I actually think I was on the money!”
That’s not to present this music as overly cerebral polemic – ‘Evil Heat’ in particular has moments of uplifting grace. Take Kate Moss’ angelic turn on a cover of ‘Some Velvet Morning’, for example. “We decided we were a track short,” he recalls, “so me and Andrew thought, let’s do a cover, and Kate can sing i.”
“Andrew wanted ‘Love Hurts’, the version by Gram Parsons and Emmylou Harris. I went for ‘Some Velvet Morning’. It was dissolute supermodel meets dissolute rock singer… but with electronics.”
There’s even a cameo from Led Zeppelin icon Robert Plant , who plays harmonica. “We met him in a pub after finishing the session with Kate Moss,” Bobby recalls. “Me being me, I just went up to him! I just said look, we’ve got this song which is a mixture between Throbbing Gristle and Howlin’ Wolf, do you want to play on it? And he did!”
Looking back doesn’t come easily to Bobby Gillespie. For one, some of the people mentioned aren’t with us any more – Mani passed away last year, for example. “I don’t sit about listening to old Primal Scream songs,” he points out during our chat. “I’m trying to write the newest Primal Scream song.”
“This re-issue gives me the chance to listen back to the albums, the B-sides… and I’ve got to say, I’m very proud of what we did. I think we wrote, produced, and released records with honour.”
“We did what a band is supposed to do: challenge themselves and challenge their audience.”
‘The Bunker trilogy’ is out now. Catch Primal Scream on the road this year.
Words: Robin Murray Photo Credit: Martina Hoogland Ivanow
items.title_zh: 逃离禁锢：Bobby Gillespie谈Primal Scream的无妥协时代
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Bobby Gillespie对Primal Scream乐队的看法，认为该乐队的音乐是对当时英国音乐的反叛。他强调，乐队成员始终追随内心的声音，而非与其他乐队竞争。Bobby Gillespie提到，在创作过程中，Primal Scream不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达，力求创作出最新的Primal Scream歌曲。这种态度体现了他们对音乐的真诚和对艺术的坚持。
items.l1_lead: Primal Scream乐队通过追随内心声音和无拘无束的创作态度，展现了对音乐的真诚和对艺术的坚持，成为当时英国音乐的反叛象征。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了Bobby Gillespie对Primal Scream乐队的看法，强调该乐队的音乐是一种对当时英国音乐的反叛。Gillespie指出，Primal Scream的成员始终忠于内心的声音，而不是与其他乐队进行竞争。这种独特的创作理念使得他们在音乐创作过程中不受传统束缚，追求独特的音乐表达，力求创作出最新的Primal Scream歌曲。

Gillespie的观点反映了乐队对音乐的真诚态度和对艺术的坚持。他们的音乐不仅仅是为了迎合市场或流行趋势，而是源于对自我表达的渴望和对音乐本质的探索。这种无妥协的态度使得Primal Scream在音乐界中独树一帜，成为一种文化现象。

通过对Primal Scream的分析，Gillespie强调了艺术创作中的自由与个性的重要性，认为只有在摆脱外界压力和传统束缚的情况下，艺术家才能真正实现自我。这种理念不仅适用于音乐领域，也对其他艺术形式有着深远的影响，鼓励艺术家们勇于追求自己的创作道路，展现真实的自我。总之，Primal Scream的音乐不仅是对当时音乐环境的反叛，更是对艺术创作自由的坚定捍卫。

items.article_body:
Department of Environmental Systems Science Services Student portal Alumni association Staffnet Login Search Search en EN DE Departments ETH Zurich D-USYS Language Selection en English Deutsch You are here Homepage News & Events News Archive 2026 09 NCCR CLIM+: Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland NCCR CLIM+: Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland With the official launch of the National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) CLIM+, researchers, public authorities, businesses and organisations are joining forces to strengthen Switzerland's resilience to climate extremes. Co-led by ETH Zurich and the University of Bern, the NCCR combines climate research with practical solutions for society, the economy and policymaking.
The National Centre of Competence in Research (NCCR) is jointly directed by Prof. Sonia I. Seneviratne (ETH Zurich) and Prof. Karin Ingold (University of Bern), with Prof. David N. Bresch and Prof. Olivia Romppainen-Martius serving as deputy co-directors. CLIM+ brings together 47 research groups from 13 Swiss institutions and works closely with public authorities, businesses and civil society organisations. "Our vision is to investigate the main challenges Switzerland faces with increasing global warming and to help develop solutions for both climate change mitigation and adaptation," says Sonia Seneviratne. "This is only possible together with society."
A key element of the programme is the development of climate storylines: interdisciplinary narratives that combine scientific knowledge and societal perspectives to explore how extreme events could unfold and how risks can be managed.
CLIM+ strengthens a research area of growing societal importance. The programme combines climate science, risk modelling and decision analysis to support informed decision-making and long-term resilience. "CLIM+ shifts the approach from reacting to isolated extremes to systematically preparing for plausible future risks," explains David N. Bresch.
At the kick-off event, representatives from science, government and practice highlighted the importance of translating research into action, from climate-resilient infrastructure and water management to governance and emergency preparedness. Speakers also stressed that adaptation alone is not enough and must be accompanied by ambitious climate mitigation efforts.
Looking ahead, CLIM+ aims to create lasting bridges between research, policy and society while contributing knowledge that supports Switzerland's climate-risk strategies and strengthens dialogue between science and the public.
The external page NCCR CLIM+ (Climate Extremes and Society: Strengthening Resilience) receives CHF 16.88 million in federal funding and additional support from ETH Zurich and the University of Bern. Researchers from D-USYS involved in the programme include Nicolas Gruber, Andreas Prein, Erich Fischer, Manuela Brunner, Reto Knutti, Tina Schnadt Poberaj, Lukas Gudmundsson and Ulrike Lohmann. external page Kick-off for a more climate-resilient Switzerland , Article from Uni Bern, 15.09.2026

items.title_zh: NCCR CLIM+: 启动更具气候韧性的瑞士
items.summary_zh: NCCR CLIM+项目旨在研究瑞士在全球变暖加剧背景下面临的主要挑战，并与社会共同开发应对气候变化的缓解（mitigation）和适应（adaptation）解决方案。项目强调，只有通过社会的共同努力，才能有效应对气候变化带来的影响。
items.l1_lead: NCCR CLIM+项目强调，瑞士应对气候变化的挑战需要社会共同努力，开发有效的缓解和适应解决方案。
items.l2_summary:
NCCR CLIM+项目旨在深入研究瑞士在全球变暖加剧背景下面临的主要挑战，并与社会各界共同开发应对气候变化的缓解（mitigation）和适应（adaptation）解决方案。该项目强调，面对气候变化带来的影响，单靠科学界或政府的努力是远远不够的，必须依靠社会的共同努力，才能有效应对这一全球性问题。通过与社会各界的合作，NCCR CLIM+项目希望能够整合不同领域的知识与资源，推动瑞士在气候韧性方面的提升。

在研究过程中，NCCR CLIM+项目将聚焦于气候变化对瑞士的具体影响，包括生态系统、经济和社会结构等多个方面。项目团队将通过数据收集和分析，识别出瑞士在气候变化背景下的脆弱环节，并提出相应的解决方案。这些解决方案不仅包括技术层面的创新，还涉及政策制定、公众参与和教育等多方面的综合措施，以确保应对气候变化的策略能够被广泛接受和有效实施。

项目的核心论点是，气候变化的影响是复杂且多维的，只有通过跨学科的合作与社会的广泛参与，才能找到切实可行的应对之道。NCCR CLIM+项目的成功实施，将为瑞士在应对气候变化的过程中提供重要的理论支持和实践指导，助力瑞士在全球气候治理中发挥更为积极的作用。通过这一项目，瑞士不仅能够提升自身的气候韧性，还能为其他国家提供宝贵的经验和借鉴，推动全球范围内的气候行动。

items.title: 'Tragedy on so many levels': PM reacts to ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday's death - standard.co.uk
items.body:
原话：“He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life, and he wasn’t coping with the loss of his career, the loss of his reputation, and he felt he couldn’t go on.”
论点：Jason Arday因职业和声誉的丧失而感到无法继续生活。

items.topic_zh: 对Jason Arday的悲痛与反思
items.claim_zh: Jason Arday因职业和声誉的丧失而感到无法继续生活。
items.article_body:
David Hughes | Izzie Addison | Michael Howie , Senior News Editor 15 August 2026 News Briefings
Get our award-winning daily news email featuring exclusive stories, opinion and expert analysis
I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice .
Andy Burnham has called the death of former Cambridge professor Jason Arday a “tragedy” that should be a “moment for reflection”.
Prof Arday, who resigned after a plagiarism row, was pronounced dead after emergency services were called an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday to reports that a man had been found unresponsive inside a property.
He told a friend he “couldn’t go on” hours before he died after being subjected to intense scrutiny over his academic career.
The Prime Minister told reporters during a visit to Cornwall: “It’s a tragedy on so many levels, but particularly just for everybody who knew Jason, his family obviously, his friends. We think of think of them today.
“It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgment. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how how things came to this.
“A really sad, sad and sorry state of affairs and I think we all today think of Jason, his contribution, and his family and friends.”
Jason Arday was found dead on Friday ES Prof Arday said he felt he “couldn’t go on” hours before he died, a friend revealed earlier on Saturday.
Prof Arday was pronounced dead after emergency services were called to Daley Thompson Way, in Battersea , just after 3pm on Friday to reports that a man had been found unresponsive inside a property.
The Metropolitan Police said his death is being treated as unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious.
Prof Arday last week resigned as professor of sociology of education at Cambridge .
A series of media reports alleged he plagiarised his PhD thesis – completed at Liverpool John Moores University – and other research.
Further questions were asked in the press about the truth of other claims he made, including saying he ran 600 miles in six days and that he had raised £5.5 million for charity.
Ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday found dead at south London address
London bus drivers 'passing out' due to extreme heat
Historic Hackney pub battles lone resident over late hours bid
Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style
An investigation at Liverpool John Moores University cleared Prof Arday of wrongdoing.
University of Cambridge professor, and director of the Autism Research Centre, Sir Simon Baron-Cohen told the BBC he spoke to Prof Arday on Friday morning.
Jason Arday was a professor of sociology of education at Cambridge University AFP/Getty Sir Simon told Radio 4’s Today programme: “He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life, and he wasn’t coping with the loss of his career, the loss of his reputation, and he felt he couldn’t go on.”
“He used those words in voice notes,” he added.
Sir Simon said: “At the heart of all of this was a man who’d been diagnosed in childhood with disabilities that included autism and language delay and learning differences.
“He was a vulnerable child, a vulnerable teenager, and a vulnerable adult, so he needed and deserved safeguarding and support and reasonable adjustment every step of the way.”
Sir Simon said Prof Arday was a “kind and gentle” man who had been “bombarded by every media outlet” and used as a “lightning rod” to examine diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policies.
Sir Simon told the BBC that plagiarism allegations made by another academic, Nathan Cofnas – who has reportedly defined himself as a “race realist” – opened up a “media frenzy”.
He said: “Jason was being used as almost like a lightning rod to examine this policy of DEI, and Jason was bombarded by every media outlet to paint him as a fraud.”
The cognitive neuroscientist said he had grown concerned about the mental health of Prof Arday, a “vulnerable autistic man” that he could see was struggling.
Andy Burnham spoke about Jason Arday’s tragic death on a visit to Cornwall on Saturday PA Sir Simon said: “In the last 10 days, I’ve witnessed his mental health getting worse and worse, as the media didn’t stop ridiculing him, humiliating him, discrediting him.
“As I said, yesterday morning, his last voice note was that he just couldn’t go on.
“We need to let the investigations proceed, we need to understand how this tragedy has happened, but there has to be accountability at lots of levels.”
In a statement on Saturday, National Education Union (NEU) general secretary Daniel Kebede said Prof Arday had been subjected to “a public and brutal takedown that unleashed a tirade of racism”.
He added: “I don’t believe this was ever simply about ‘professional conduct’ or ‘plagiarism’.
“There is a profound difference between scrutiny and a sustained public campaign that turns an individual into a symbol of everything the right believes is wrong with DEI.
“The effect has been chilling. It tells black people and others from underrepresented backgrounds that entering prominent public positions will make you a target.
“A target not only for criticism of your work, but for a much broader political and cultural backlash.”

items.title_zh: 前剑桥教授杰森·阿尔代去世引发的多重悲剧
items.summary_zh: 杰森·阿尔代（Jason Arday）因职业和声誉的丧失而感到无法继续生活。他在生前遭受了无情的审视，包括嘲笑和对他生活每个细节的抹黑，导致他无法应对失去事业和声誉的痛苦。正如一位评论者所言，他感到无法继续前行，这反映了学术界对个人生活的影响及其潜在的悲剧性后果。阿尔代的去世不仅是个人的悲剧，也引发了对学术环境中压力和心理健康问题的深刻反思。
items.l1_lead: 杰森·阿尔代的去世揭示了学术界对个人生活的影响及其导致的心理健康危机，反映出职业压力可能引发的悲剧性后果。
items.l2_summary: 杰森·阿尔代（Jason Alday）的去世引发了对学术界压力和心理健康问题的深刻反思。他在生前因职业和声誉的丧失而感到绝望，无法继续生活。阿尔代遭受了无情的审视，包括嘲笑和对他生活每个细节的抹黑，这些都加剧了他对失去事业和声誉的痛苦。正如一位评论者所指出的，他感到无法继续前行，这一现象反映了学术界对个人生活的影响及其潜在的悲剧性后果。阿尔代的去世不仅是他个人的悲剧，也揭示了学术环境中普遍存在的压力和心理健康问题，促使人们重新审视这一领域对学者的影响。学术界的竞争和对个人生活的过度关注，可能导致严重的心理健康问题，甚至悲剧的发生。阿尔代的经历提醒我们，学术界需要更加关注研究人员的心理健康，创造一个更为支持和理解的环境，以防止类似悲剧的重演。

items.title_zh: 林赛·克兰西案背后的黑暗心理学
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了林赛·克兰西（Lindsay Clancy）案中可能涉及的心理健康问题。专家指出，克兰西的行为可能符合边缘性人格障碍（Borderline Personality Disorder）的五个特征，这足以进行诊断。具体而言，她的行为表现出自杀倾向和情绪调节困难等特征。这些心理特征为理解她的行为提供了重要的背景，揭示了在极端情况下，心理健康问题如何影响个体的决策和行为。
items.l1_lead: 林赛·克兰西案揭示了边缘性人格障碍对个体决策和行为的深远影响，尤其在极端心理健康问题下。
items.l2_summary: 林赛·克兰西案引发了对其心理健康问题的深入探讨，专家们认为她的行为可能符合边缘性人格障碍（Borderline Personality Disorder）的五个特征，这为对她的行为进行诊断提供了依据。具体而言，克兰西表现出自杀倾向和情绪调节困难等特征，这些心理特征为理解她在极端情况下的决策和行为提供了重要的背景。边缘性人格障碍通常与情绪不稳定、冲动行为和人际关系困难等相关，克兰西的案例突显了心理健康问题如何在关键时刻影响个体的选择和行为。通过分析她的行为，专家们揭示了心理健康问题在极端情境下的潜在影响，强调了对心理健康的关注和干预的重要性。这一案例不仅引发了对克兰西个人心理状态的思考，也促使社会对心理健康问题的重视，尤其是在面临压力和危机时，心理健康问题可能导致的严重后果。

items.title: Hawaii to Put Thirty Years of Eucalyptus Through Load Testing - Wood Central
items.body:
原话：“We can help create a more resilient local building supply.”
论点：他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
论据：Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.authors: Jun Wang
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Wood Central） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: We can help create a more resilient local building supply.
items.topic_zh: 关于增强当地建筑材料供应的观点
items.claim_zh: 他认为通过研究可以增强夏威夷的建筑材料供应的韧性。
items.evidence_zh: Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing.
items.article_body:
Eucalyptus stands across more than 34,000 acres of Hawaiʻi’s old sugar land, or 13,760 hectares, and no published data exists to tell a builder what a plank of lumber can hold. However, that could soon change thanks to a new University of Hawaiʻi project , which will see the USDA Forest Service provide US$300,000 to generate structural design values for the species, with the project to fell the trees, saw the boards, and test them.
“We can help create a more resilient local building supply,” said Jun Wang, an assistant professor in the university’s Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering, whose team will run the work with state agencies, forest landowners, and industry partners. Wang has taken an additional $8,000 from the American Society for Engineering Education to incorporate the same material into civil engineering coursework at Mānoa.
Hawaiʻi’s large landowners put those trees into former cane land through the 1990s, holding tens of thousands of Hāmakua Coast acres off the property market , with agreements drawn to sell the crop to Oji Paper and Marubeni , the Japanese consortium that would chip it for paper. Hawaiian authorities rejected a 1997 lease over 4,150 hectares of public land after local opposition. The ventures that followed came and went, and the trees stayed.
Engineers cannot specify a beam without published design values, and no building official approves a species for load-bearing work until those numbers exist, regardless of what the timber does in a test rig. Eucalyptus grandis and E. saligna dominate the Hāmakua stands, which Mālama Hāmakua reports foresters rate suitable for flooring, structural, veneer, and ply work.
Distributors on the islands hold two to four weeks of stock compared with eight to 12 weeks on the mainland, so a West Coast price rise reaches an island invoice inside a fortnight, according to Associated Builders and Contractors Hawaiʻi. The same association puts local sourcing at under 20 per cent of the state’s building material needs, with the balance requiring an ocean crossing before reaching a site.
No mill on Hawaiʻi Island runs at the scale that would put eucalyptus boards alongside imported product on price, and the island’s hardwood mills stay with high-value koa to turn a profit, on Mālama Hāmakua’s account of what foresters told it. The wood that did leave between 2012 and 2016 went to China as veneer material before that market fell away, and a Waiakea mill licensed to peel the species never reached the volumes proposed.
It comes as Australian researchers turned plantation bluegum grown for pulp into structural glulam in February, the same class of timber used for the same purpose, with a Portland hub costing $200 million proposed to make the product at scale. Grading the timber and building the mill are separate bills, and only the first has been funded in Hawaiʻi.
Fire has given the state a second argument for cutting the stands, with the Department of Land and Natural Resources estimating that the 2012 Kōkeʻe wildfires released 72,000 tonnes of carbon, which it compares to the annual emissions of 18,000 cars. Those fires burned more than 3,000 acres of a Timber Management Area that covers 17,092 acres and holds more than 1,600 acres of eucalyptus and pine.
The department built a house from these species eight years ago, with Hale Liʻi framed in Sydney gum, rose gum, and southern yellow pine cut from Kōkeʻe on Kauaʻi and Hāmakua on Hawaiʻi Island. That 2018 grant came from the same federal Wood Innovations programme, and the 400-square-foot result is one nobody can yet repeat at commercial scale.
Wang’s team has $300,000 to produce numbers no one has generated over the three decades those trees have been standing, on an estate the university puts at over 34,000 acres. Design values will settle whether Hawaiʻi’s eucalyptus can be built with, and a mill will settle whether it ever is.
items.title_zh: 夏威夷将对三十年桉树进行负载测试
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了夏威夷的一项研究计划，旨在通过对三十年生桉树（Eucalyptus）的负载测试，增强当地建筑材料的韧性。研究团队由Wang领导，获得了30万美元的资金，计划生成过去三十年未曾获得的数据。这项研究的核心论点是，通过科学研究可以提升夏威夷建筑材料供应的韧性，从而为当地建筑行业提供更可靠的材料支持。
items.l1_lead: 夏威夷研究团队将对三十年桉树进行负载测试，以提升当地建筑材料的韧性，为建筑行业提供更可靠的材料支持。
items.l2_summary: 夏威夷的一项研究计划正在进行，旨在通过对三十年生桉树（Eucalyptus）进行负载测试，以增强当地建筑材料的韧性。该研究由Wang教授领导，获得了30万美元的资金支持，计划生成过去三十年未曾获得的数据。这项研究的核心论点是，通过科学研究可以提升夏威夷建筑材料的韧性，从而为当地建筑行业提供更可靠的材料支持。研究团队希望通过对桉树的负载测试，获取有关其物理特性和性能的数据，这些数据将为建筑材料的选择和应用提供重要的科学依据。通过这一研究，夏威夷的建筑行业将能够在材料的选择上更加科学和合理，进而提高建筑的安全性和耐用性。总之，这项研究不仅有助于填补过去三十年在建筑材料韧性方面的数据空白，还将为夏威夷的建筑行业带来积极的影响。

items.title: Surely Liberals Can Agree That Plagiarism Is Bad - persuasion.community
items.body:
原话：“1 in 4 autistic people have planned or attempted suicide. That’s why I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Professor Jason Arday who is autistic.”
论点：他对自闭症人士的关注是因为1/4的自闭症患者曾计划或尝试自杀。
items.authors: Simon Baron‐Cohen
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（persuasion.community） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: 1 in 4 autistic people have planned or attempted suicide. That’s why I’m very concerned about the impact of the media coverage on Professor Jason Arday who is autistic.
items.topic_zh: 对自闭症人士媒体报道影响的关注
items.claim_zh: 他对自闭症人士的关注是因为1/4的自闭症患者曾计划或尝试自杀。
items.article_body:
Sam Kahn Aug 03, 2026 373 15 58 Share Cambridge University’s Senate House. (Photo by Joe Giddens/PA Images via Getty Images.) This is a nasty story.
In 2023, Jason Arday made international news for becoming, at age 37, the youngest black professor in the history of Cambridge University. It wasn’t just that, though. Arday had a really remarkable background. Raised on a council estate in south London, Arday was, in his account, diagnosed at age three with autism and global development delay and didn’t speak until he was 11. At that point, something “clicked,” as he has put it, but he wouldn’t read or write until he was 18.
Then, Arday really applied himself. By age 30, he obtained a Ph.D. in Educational Studies from Liverpool John Moores University, and, according to his official biography , worked at Roehampton, Durham, and Glasgow before being appointed to a highly prestigious professorship at Cambridge. In his spare time, Arday was an ultra long-distance runner, in 2010 completing 30 marathons in 35 days and over two decades raising £5.5 million for charity.
It’s a beautiful story—Arday himself for the documentary “Great Big Story” said of his life, “Wouldn’t it be the most ridiculous story ever told?”—and it’s about to be commemorated in a memoir that Simon & Schuster UK is releasing later this month.
The only problem is that large portions of it may not be true.
In 2023, only months after his appointment at Cambridge, a pair of academics, Dave Harris and Martyn Hammersley, raised concerns to Cambridge, to Liverpool John Moores, and to different journals Arday had published in about the academic integrity of Arday’s work. Two of the journals issued corrections . Cambridge replied that the issues preceded Arday’s hiring and therefore were not within Cambridge’s “remit” to investigate. Liverpool John Moores, for its part, has issued a statement that the university in 2025 conducted a “confidential procedure” in response to the allegations and that “Professor Arday’s PhD still stands.”
Persuasion is a registered nonprofit that relies on reader support to pay our staff and keep our content free for everyone. If you value our work and want to fight for liberal values wherever they are threatened, please become a paying subscriber today!
In 2025, the Times Higher Education spiked an article about the allegations against Arday after Arday enlisted the defamation law firm Carter-Ruck to send a letter to the publication. But last month, Nathan Cofnas, a former Fellow at Cambridge, published a post on Substack that blew the Arday story wide open. Using the plagiarism detector Copyleaks, Cofnas found over 30 cases of “substantial overlap” in Arday’s Ph.D. dissertation with the previously-published dissertation of Paula Zwozdiak-Myers , many of them long chunks of verbatim copying, as well as verbatim copying from other sources. Cofnas went through ten other papers of Arday’s, taken from Arday’s own list of “principal and recent publications,” and found significant issues, including plagiarism, in at least four of them. Additional malfeasance included virtually identical quotes attributed to different sources in different papers, which strongly implies that at least some of the quotes from supposed participants in his studies were confabulated .
Meanwhile, Cofnas raised difficult questions about aspects of Arday’s personal story. He noted that running 30 marathons in 35 days would place Arday in the ultra-marathon elite—this without having left any ostensible mark in the running community. “If Arday [did that], I’ll eat my yarmulke,” said Cofnas by telephone. The claim to have raised £5.5 million for charity has already been walked back by Arday, who in a recent interview said the fundraising was done in conjunction with collectives. And Cofnas found that Arday’s two GCSE qualifications—in physical education and textiles—were unobtainable without passing written tests, a detail that challenges the timeline given by Arday that he could not read or write until he was 18. Cofnas also suggests that Arday’s account of his speech development is “medically improbable.”
Cofnas is far from a neutral party in this case. He was fired by Cambridge’s Emmanuel College in 2024 on the back of student protests against him for a Substack post in which he wrote that in a color-blind meritocracy “blacks would disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment.” Harris, the academic who first raised questions about Arday’s scholarship, was embroiled in a controversy of his own in which he had his emeritus title at Plymouth Marjon University stripped for a time after he critiqued critical race theory.
How To Fix DEI Rachel Kleinfeld · September 26, 2024 Read full story The fact that his accusers are controversial in their own right may help to explain why so many academics have reflexively defended Arday. In an interview with The Times of London, Arday this week said , “There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position. The motive is racially motivated. I think there’s a reason why it’s me, and I do think that reason is aligned to ableism and racism.” In 2025, when the allegations against Arday were beginning to surface, the Cambridge professors Simon Baron-Cohen and Ricardo Sabates circulated an open letter under the heading “URGENT PLEASE SIGN ANTI-RACISM LETTER FOR JASON ARDAY.” The Good Law Project, an activist organization, orchestrated a solidarity letter last week that has been signed by 14,000 people decrying the “sustained and malicious attacks on the academic integrity of Dr. Jason Arday,” which the letter attributed to “an attempt to undermine Black people who hold positions of influence.” And Cambridge University has wholeheartedly taken Arday’s side. A university spokesperson said , “Professor Arday has been the victim of a vile campaign to undermine his credibility, which must stop.”
So—as you can see—it’s an uncomfortable story landing right on the faultlines of the culture wars. On one side is institutional procedure alongside an institutional culture hyper-sensitive to accusations against what the Good Law Project calls “a working class Black man.” On the other side is the argument that standards must be maintained—and maintained by academic and journalistic vigilantes if the institutions are unwilling to uphold their own meritocratic principles.
And of course the real issue isn’t exactly Arday. It’s the presumption that the politically progressive culture ascendant at Cambridge and in higher education in general has long ago deviated from real meritocracy. By phone, Cofnas was clear on that point. He said, “This is a story about DEI and the corruption that is required to sustain the system of DEI—of elevating people based on identity characteristics rather than merit.”
So what do we do in a case like this, where everybody pretty much sees what they are already predisposed to see? Well, first of all, we look at the source material—and in this case it’s pretty unequivocal. For instance, Arday’s line on page 17 of his 2015 dissertation—“Student teachers are unique individuals and differ in their personal biographies and prior experiences, disposition to enquiry, cognitive and perceptive abilities, communication, interpersonal skills, adaptability, values, and belief systems”—is a perfect match to page 1 of Zwozdiak-Myers’ 2009 dissertation . According to Cofnas, the pattern is repeated dozens of times, while The Telegraph for its part found “more than 100 passages that are identical or nearly identical” to Zwozdiak-Myers’ thesis. There is, as Harris put it , “no other plausible explanation” than plagiarism for the overlaps.
Then, in the week following Cofnas’ Substack post, subsequent reporting found additional patterns of fabulism by Arday. In an open letter to a government minister last year, Arday said he was the victim of innumerable threats and attacks since he took up his Cambridge position. In an interview with The Guardian this week, Arday clarified that he was referring to, among other incidents, a “severed pig’s head” that had been sent to his parents’ London home. That assertion triggered a macabre scavenger hunt, with Guardian journalists visiting the butcher shop that Arday claimed had sold the pig to the assailant. But the butcher said that there had been no police investigation into the incident, as Arday had asserted. For their part, London’s Metropolitan Police said that the details Arday gave of a police investigation into the incident were “categorically” inaccurate.
Arday further claimed that a masked man had accosted him twice at his Cambridge faculty building and threatened him with a knife the second time. But as The Guardian noted, no intruder appeared on CCTV on either occasion, and Arday did not inform colleagues or interrupt his working day after the alleged knife incident.
Meanwhile, a recently-surfaced video interview with Arday appears to show him claiming that he starred in the acclaimed documentary “Seven Up”—a mathematical impossibility unless Arday was actually born in 1956. And just today Glasgow University has denied Arday’s claim that he held a visiting professorship there.
Given all that—the all-but-indisputable evidence of plagiarism, in addition to the patterns of fanciful statements by Arday—the case for his defense collapses. “I think it’s plagiarism and it’s obvious,” one academic told The Guardian under condition of anonymity. “There is no question that there is extensive plagiarism,” David Sanders, an independent researcher who reviewed Arday’s case last year for Times Higher Education , said to Retraction Watch.
What Being a Digital Nomad Taught Me About the Real World Sam Kahn · Jul 27 Read full story Arday, for his part, did not, in a wide-ranging interview he gave to The Times of London last week, directly challenge the primary allegation of plagiarism and academic misconduct. He said, “I am accountable for the mistakes I’ve made. I hold myself accountable and other people should hold me accountable.” Instead, he took another line of defense, contending, “We’re talking about academia here. I didn’t murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I’ve experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable.”
If it’s fair to say that the preponderance of evidence at this point speaks to serious academic misconduct on Arday’s part, the next question—picking up on Arday’s lead—is to ask ourselves what the stakes are here and what the story is really about. Arday is right of course that one academic with a shaky relationship to the truth is not, by itself, a huge deal. But, unfortunately for Arday’s defense, it is a story with more reach than he admits and it really does indict the institutions backing him.
For one thing, there is the issue of how Arday and his supporters have tried to defend him. There has been very little of the accountability Arday has called for—and there has been no willingness to look at the very obvious evidence of academic misconduct. The overriding tendency has been to shoot the messenger and to go after the academics, particularly Harris and Cofnas, who called attention to the issues in Arday’s work. According to The Guardian, Arday attempted to lodge a police complaint against Harris. Earlier this year, he dedicated a talk at the British Sociological Association to the “playbook” employed by conservative activists to target black professors. “There isn’t any room to sit there and watch your fellows suffer for no reason. It’s abhorrent, it’s a disgrace and, quite frankly, evil,” Arday said .
Apart from the often vitriolic counter-attack against Arday’s accusers, there has been a tendency to dodge the issue and shield Arday through arguments related to his neurodivergence. “1 in 4 autistic people have planned or attempted suicide. That’s why I’m very concerned about the impa
items.title_zh: 自闭症患者自杀风险引发关注
items.summary_zh: 文章提到，自闭症患者中有四分之一曾计划或尝试自杀，这一数据引发了对媒体报道影响的担忧。作者以自闭症人士Jason Arday为例，强调了对自闭症群体的关注，指出媒体在报道时应更加谨慎，以避免对这一脆弱群体产生负面影响。文章核心论点在于，社会应重视自闭症患者的心理健康问题，并采取措施降低自杀风险。
items.l1_lead: 自闭症患者中四分之一曾计划或尝试自杀，呼吁社会关注其心理健康并谨慎对待媒体报道。
items.l2_summary: 自闭症患者的心理健康问题日益受到关注，尤其是自杀风险的显著性引发了社会的广泛讨论。根据研究数据显示，约有四分之一的自闭症患者曾计划或尝试自杀，这一惊人的比例引起了人们对媒体报道的深刻反思。文章以自闭症人士Jason Arday为例，强调了对自闭症群体的关注，指出媒体在报道相关事件时应更加谨慎，以避免对这一脆弱群体产生负面影响。自闭症患者面临的心理健康挑战不仅影响他们的生活质量，也对社会的整体福祉构成威胁。因此，社会各界应当重视自闭症患者的心理健康问题，采取有效措施降低自杀风险。通过提高公众对自闭症的理解和支持，改善相关服务和资源的可获得性，可以为自闭症患者创造一个更安全、更包容的环境。总之，关注自闭症患者的心理健康，尤其是自杀风险，是社会责任的体现，亟需引起更多的重视和行动。

items.title: Comparison between accelerated and standard or sham rTMS in the treatment of depression: A systematic review.
items.body: Major depressive disorder (MDD) represents a major global health challenge, with a significant proportion of patients being resistant to drug treatment (TRD). Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has shown promise in the treatment of MDD/TRD, with a single stimulation session per day for five days per week over several weeks (the "standard" protocol). The two main paradigms used are high-frequency rTMS and intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) delivered to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Accelerated TMS (aTMS) protocols aim to make the treatment more effective, or at least more rapidly effective, by delivering more stimulations in a shorter time, which could also facilitate the implementation of the protocols for a larger number of patients. In this systematic literature review, articles comparing in the same study an aTMS protocol to a standard or sham rTMS protocol were retained for analysis. Thus, 23 articles were retained and the analysis focused on the efficacy of aTMS protocols used for the treatment of depression (MDD/TRD) as well as on the impact of various stimulation parameters, such as stimulation pattern, intersession interval, dosage, and methods of cortical targeting. Although some studies did not report significant differences between aTMS and standard or sham protocols, others suggested potential advantages of aTMS, such as twice-daily HF-rTMS of the left DLPFC or more intensive iTBS protocols with a long interval between two sessions and personalized cortical targeting. Our results highlight the influence of the number of sessions or pulses per session (dosage), the duration of the interval between sessions, and the precision of target localization (using image-guided neuronavigation) on therapeutic efficacy. However, limitations in sample size, few independent studies replicating the same methodology, and variability in the clinical profile of treated patients, given different definitions of treatment resistance or the presence of comorbidities, hamper definitive conclusions.

items.title_zh: 加速与标准或假刺激rTMS治疗抑郁症的比较研究
items.summary_zh: 重度抑郁障碍（MDD）是全球健康的重要挑战，部分患者对药物治疗（TRD）产生抵抗。重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）在MDD/TRD治疗中展现出希望，标准方案为每周五天每天一次的刺激。主要使用的两种方案为高频rTMS和间歇性θ波刺激（iTBS），针对左侧背外侧前额叶皮层（DLPFC）。加速TMS（aTMS）方案旨在通过在更短时间内提供更多刺激，提高治疗效果或加快效果，从而使更多患者受益。本系统文献综述分析了23篇比较aTMS与标准或假刺激rTMS的研究，重点关注aTMS在抑郁症（MDD/TRD）治疗中的有效性及刺激参数的影响。尽管部分研究未发现aTMS与标准或假刺激方案之间的显著差异，但其他研究则指出aTMS可能具有潜在优势。
items.l1_lead: 加速TMS（aTMS）在治疗重度抑郁障碍中显示出潜在优势，尽管部分研究未发现其与标准或假刺激方案的显著差异。
items.l2_summary:
重度抑郁障碍（MDD）是全球健康面临的重要挑战，部分患者对药物治疗（TRD）产生抵抗，导致治疗效果不佳。重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）作为一种新兴的治疗手段，在MDD/TRD的治疗中展现出希望。标准的rTMS治疗方案通常为每周五天、每天一次，主要采用高频rTMS和间歇性θ波刺激（iTBS），针对左侧背外侧前额叶皮层（DLPFC）。为了提高治疗效果或加快效果，加速TMS（aTMS）方案应运而生，旨在通过在更短时间内提供更多刺激，使更多患者受益。

本系统文献综述分析了23篇比较aTMS与标准或假刺激rTMS的研究，重点关注aTMS在抑郁症（MDD/TRD）治疗中的有效性及刺激参数的影响。尽管部分研究未发现aTMS与标准或假刺激方案之间存在显著差异，但其他研究则指出，aTMS可能具有潜在的优势，尤其是在治疗效果的加速方面。这些研究的结果表明，aTMS在某些情况下可能能够更快地改善患者的抑郁症状，从而为临床治疗提供了新的思路。

综上所述，尽管目前的研究结果并不完全一致，但aTMS作为一种新兴的治疗方案，仍然显示出在抑郁症治疗中的潜力，值得进一步的深入研究和临床应用。通过对不同刺激参数的探索，未来可能会找到更有效的治疗策略，以帮助更多的抑郁症患者获得改善。

items.title: Executive functioning in adolescents with internalizing disorders: a systematic review.
items.body: Internalizing disorders (INTs), including anxiety (AD) and depressive disorders (DD), frequently emerge during adolescence. Studies suggest that certain core domains of executive functioning (EF), i.e. inhibition, shifting and working memory (WM) may show selectively lower performance in certain INTs. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the evidence of associations between INTs and EF in adolescents. A systematic search was conducted in Medline, Psych-INFO, Scopus, and Web of Science in May 2023. Inclusion focused on adolescents (12-17) with AD (including obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)) or DD. After screening 2,551 titles/abstracts, 818 records underwent full-text review, on which independent reviewers reached 93% agreement on eligibility. EF parameters, measured through task-performance or ratings, were extracted from 32 eligible articles published since 2014. Performance-based EF differences were reported in 22 studies, most frequently in adolescents with DD. Task-based inhibition showed lower scores most consistently in DD (n = 5). Findings were mixed across other INTs. Three studies found evidence for improved inhibition performance in OCD (n = 2) and AD (n = 1). Finally, 6 studies reporting on self- or parent-rated EF found significant difficulties across EF domains, of which 3 contrasted with intact performances on task-based measurements of EF. Findings suggest both objective and subjective EF difficulties across INTs with no conclusive evidence for selective domain-specific differences. We highlight a discrepancy between subjectively experienced or observed deficits in daily EF and performance on structured tasks. This suggests that rating-based EF may be more sensitive for capturing subtle EF difficulties and therefore adds value in research and clinical settings. Finally, the quality of studies is discussed and directions for future studies are identified, namely, the use of both task and rating-based measures of EF as well as inclusion of larger sample sizes.
items.authors: Fontaine GP, Blake KV, Koen N, Stein DJ, Hammar Å, Groenewold NA.
items.title_zh: 青少年内化障碍与执行功能的系统评估
items.summary_zh: 内化障碍（INTs），包括焦虑障碍（AD）和抑郁障碍（DD），常在青少年时期出现。本系统评估旨在探讨青少年内化障碍与执行功能（EF）之间的关联。通过在2023年5月对Medline、Psych-INFO、Scopus和Web of Science进行系统检索，纳入了12至17岁患有AD（包括强迫症（OCD）和创伤后应激障碍（PTSD））或DD的青少年。经过筛选，共有32篇自2014年以来的符合条件的文章被纳入，EF参数通过任务表现或评分进行测量。22项研究报告了基于表现的EF差异，尤其在DD青少年中最为明显。任务基础的抑制能力在DD中表现出较低的得分（n = 5）。其他内化障碍的结果则较为混杂。三项研究发现OCD（n = 2）和AD（n = 1）在抑制表现上有所改善。最后，6项关于自评或家长评估的研究发现EF各领域存在显著困难，其中3项与任务表现的完整性相对立。
items.l1_lead: 青少年内化障碍与执行功能之间存在显著关联，尤其抑郁障碍患者在执行功能表现上较差，且自评与任务表现结果存在不一致。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在系统评估青少年内化障碍（INTs）与执行功能（EF）之间的关系，特别关注焦虑障碍（AD）和抑郁障碍（DD）。内化障碍在青少年时期常见，影响其心理健康和日常生活。研究通过对2023年5月在Medline、Psych-INFO、Scopus和Web of Science进行的系统检索，纳入了12至17岁患有AD（包括强迫症（OCD）和创伤后应激障碍（PTSD））或DD的青少年。经过筛选，共有32篇自2014年以来的符合条件的文章被纳入分析。

在这些研究中，EF的参数主要通过任务表现或评分进行测量。结果显示，22项研究报告了基于表现的EF差异，尤其在DD青少年中表现得尤为明显。具体而言，任务基础的抑制能力在DD青少年中得分较低（n = 5），表明他们在执行功能方面存在显著困难。尽管其他内化障碍的结果较为混杂，但有三项研究发现OCD（n = 2）和AD（n = 1）在抑制表现上有所改善，提示某些青少年在特定情况下可能具备一定的执行功能恢复能力。

此外，6项关于自评或家长评估的研究发现，EF各领域存在显著困难，其中3项研究的结果与任务表现的完整性相对立，进一步强调了青少年在执行功能方面的挑战。这些发现表明，内化障碍与执行功能之间存在复杂的相互关系，尤其是DD青少年在执行功能方面的表现较差，可能影响其心理健康和社会适应能力。因此，针对青少年内化障碍的干预措施应考虑到执行功能的评估与提升，以帮助他们更好地应对生活中的挑战。

items.title: A whole-brain voxel-based analysis of structural abnormalities in PTSD: An ENIGMA-PGC study.
items.body: Background Patients with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) exhibit smaller regional brain volumes in commonly reported regions including the amygdala and hippocampus, regions associated with fear and memory processing. In the current study, we have conducted a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) meta-analysis using whole-brain statistical maps with neuroimaging data from the ENIGMA-PGC PTSD working group. Methods T1-weighted structural neuroimaging scans from 36 cohorts (PTSD n = 1309; controls n = 2198) were processed using a standardized VBM pipeline (ENIGMA-VBM tool). We meta-analyzed the resulting statistical maps for voxel-wise differences in gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) volumes between PTSD patients and controls, performed subgroup analyses considering the trauma exposure of the controls, and examined associations between regional brain volumes and clinical variables including PTSD (CAPS-4/5, PCL-5) and depression severity (BDI-II, PHQ-9). Results PTSD patients exhibited smaller GM volumes across the frontal and temporal lobes, and cerebellum, with the most significant effect in the left cerebellum (Hedges' g = 0.22, p corrected = .001), and smaller cerebellar WM volume (peak Hedges' g = 0.14, p corrected = .008). We observed similar regional differences when comparing patients to trauma-exposed controls, suggesting these structural abnormalities may be specific to PTSD. Regression analyses revealed PTSD severity was negatively associated with GM volumes within the cerebellum ( p corrected = .003), while depression severity was negatively associated with GM volumes within the cerebellum and superior frontal gyrus in patients ( p corrected = .001). Conclusions PTSD patients exhibited widespread, regional differences in brain volumes where greater regional deficits appeared to reflect more severe symptoms. Our findings add to the growing literature implicating the cerebellum in PTSD psychopathology.
